(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- docs-consistency-guard: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/architecture.md. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y." (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. - migration-safety: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>

<example>

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- qa-verifier: QA/QE agent that (1) runs the full local verification battery mirroring CI's required checks before any commit/push/PR, (2) audits test quality on changed code — failure-mode coverage, mocked-seam smells, coverage on changed files (Week-8 ≥80% gate), and (3) exercises the running application with data-level scenarios — authoring suites/checks through the real API, negative and edge-case inputs, authz probes — against the local stack's seeded demo data. # Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". ## Low-hanging fruit

From the open-issue queue (`v1.1 Backlog` + Week 6/7 milestones), a few stand out as small and self-contained:

| Issue | Why it's low-hanging |
|---|---|
| **#1264** — lineage floor-denial message names the wrong grant + a `NoReturn` docstring overstates its effect | Pure text/message fix, no logic change |

state:	OPEN

labels:	priority/P3, refactor
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:

blocking:	
number:	1247
--
Follow-up filed from the `/code-review` pass on #1235 (fixes #1199). Not a correctness bug today — filed rather than dropped, per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a.

## What

`workspace_health.key` is an opaque SHA-256 hash by design: the identifying tuple `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, run_env, binding_env)` can run to ~256 chars (Airflow DAG ids) against a 64-char PK column, so there is nothing to `SELECT` a tuple back out of.

The #1199 read path (`workspace_health_service.list_current_env_near_misses`) therefore works by **re-deriving candidate tuples and hash-probing**: it enumerates every ENABLED `trigger_binding`'s `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, env)`, crosses it with the other three members of the closed `ENVS` vocabulary as candidate `run_env`s, hashes each with the same `_near_miss_key` the write side uses, and keeps the hashes that exist as real rows.

That means the read side's candidate-selection logic must stay in lock-step with the **write** side's (`orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses`) — and today the only thing coupling them is a prose comment in each. The shared code is just `_near_miss_key`; the *choice of which tuples get hashed* is duplicated.

#1235 added `TestNearMissWriteReadRoundTrip` (a test that drives the real production write path and asserts the read side decodes it, plus a disabled-binding case), which turns a future desync into a red test rather than a silent one. This issue is about removing the duplication itself.

## Options (pick at design time)

1. **Store the tuple.** Add a nullable JSONB `detail` column (or a sibling `near_miss` table) alongside the hashed key, so the read is a plain `SELECT` and no candidate derivation exists at all. Costs a migration; ends the coupling outright. Probably the right answer.
2. **Extract one shared derivation.** A single function both sides call, e.g. `candidate_near_miss_tuples(...)`, so there is exactly one definition of "which tuples are eligible."
3. Leave as-is and rely on the round-trip test.

## Also in scope (cheap, related)

`TriggersPanel` fetches near-misses on every mount with no caching. #1235 narrowed it to `?suite_id=` so it no longer pulls the whole accessible workspace on each suite switch, but it still fires for suites with zero trigger bindings (the alternative — gating the fetch on the bindings result — would serialise the two requests into a waterfall, which is worse). A shared cache across suite switches would remove the redundant call entirely.

## Acceptance

- Only one place in the codebase decides which `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, run_env, binding_env)` tuples constitute a near-miss.
- The #1235 round-trip tests still pass unchanged (they assert behaviour, not structure).

## Task: fix GitHub issue #1266

Run `gh issue view 1266` for the full text, but here's the gist:

`backend/app/db/session.py`'s `_build_engine()` and `backend/alembic/env.py`'s `run_migrations_online()` both pass psycopg2/libpq-specific `connect_args` keys (`connect_timeout`, and `keepalives`/`keepalives_idle`/`keepalives_interval`/`keepalives_count`) directly into `create_engine()`/`engine_from_config()`, with **no guard on the resolved SQLAlchemy driver**. If `settings.database_url` (which has no scheme/driver validator and is env-overridable via `DATABASE_URL`) ever resolved to a non-psycopg2 driver, the first real connection attempt would raise `TypeError` on the unrecognized kwarg at app/worker/migrate-job startup — not gracefully.

`backend/tests/conftest.py` already has a helper `_probe_postgres` that gates its own `connect_timeout` usage behind a `drivername` check — this is the pattern to mirror.

## Suggested direction (issue lists two options — pick the first, it's the smaller/safer change and mirrors existing code)

Add a driver guard (mirroring `conftest.py`'s `_probe_postgres` pattern) around the psycopg2-specific `connect_args` in BOTH `backend/app/db/session.py` and `backend/alembic/env.py`, so a non-psycopg2 driver degrades to no keepalives/connect_timeout instead of crashing at startup with an opaque `TypeError`. Read `_probe_postgres` in `backend/tests/conftest.py` first to see the exact `drivername` check pattern used (likely something like checking `sqlalchemy.engine.url.make_url(...).drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg2")` or similar — match whatever idiom is already there rather than inventing a new one).

Do NOT add a new Settings validator (that's the issue's second, more invasive option) — keep this change small and localized to the two call sites, consistent with the existing conftest precedent.

## Process (follow CLAUDE.md §6 working agreements)

1. Create a branch `fix/issue-1266-connect-args-driver-guard` off `main`.
2. Read `backend/app/db/session.py` (`_build_engine`), `backend/alembic/env.py` (`run_migrations_online`), and `backend/tests/conftest.py` (`_probe_postgres`) fully before changing anything.
3. Apply the guard in both real call sites (session.py and alembic/env.py), reusing/extracting a shared helper if that avoids duplicating the driver-check logic across three places (session.py, alembic/env.py, conftest.py already has its own) — but don't over-engineer; if the existing pattern is already small enough to just repeat twice with a comment, that's acceptable too. Use your judgment on whether a shared `backend/app/db/` utility function is warranted per the project's "no premature abstraction" rule, but three near-identical driver checks doing the same thing is a real duplication smell worth a one-function extraction if it's easy.
4. Add test coverage: a test that constructs a non-psycopg2 URL (e.g. `postgresql+asyncpg://...` or similar) and asserts `_build_engine`/`run_migrations_online`'s connect_args-building logic does NOT include the psycopg2-only keys, alongside the existing-path (psycopg2) case still including them. Check existing tests for `_build_engine` first (`backend/tests/`) to follow established test patterns/fixtures in this file.
5. Verify locally BEFORE committing: run Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit, and the relevant pytest module(s) covering `backend/app/db/session.py` and `backend/alembic/env.py` (check if alembic env.py has any existing test coverage — it may not, since it's typically exercised via `alembic upgrade head` rather than unit tests; note this in your report if so, but don't skip verifying session.py's coverage).
6. Commit with a conventional commit message (`fix: ...`), body explaining the why (psycopg2-specific connect_args passed to create_engine with no driver guard), referencing the issue.
7. Push the branch and open a PR via `gh pr create` with `Fixes #1266` in the body. Use the repo's PR template if `.github/pull_request_template.md` exists.
8. Spawn the `/code-review` skill/slash-command flow on your own diff (mandatory per this repo's working agreements — never only an inline self-review); if unavailable, use the `pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer` agent type via the Agent tool against your diff. Fix anything it finds that's in scope.
9. Do NOT merge the PR — leave it open for CI + human merge.

## Report back

In your final message: the PR URL, a one-line summary, confirmation local verification passed, and what code-review found (if anything).

## Task: fix GitHub issue #1275

Run `gh issue view 1275` for the full text, but here's the gist: three antd v6 deprecation warnings appear repeatedly in the browser console during normal UI use (found during a QA pass, no functional impact, purely console noise):

- `Modal`'s `maskClosable` prop is deprecated
- `Select`'s `onDropdownVisibleChange` prop is deprecated (antd's known replacement is `onOpenChange` — verify this against current antd docs/changelog before assuming)
- `Drawer`'s `width` prop is deprecated (seen when opening the check-history drawer)

## Process

1. Look up the actual antd v6 migration guidance for these three props before touching code — use the `claude.ai Context7 query-docs`/`resolve-library-id` MCP tools (resolve library id for "antd" or "ant-design", then query docs for "Modal maskClosable deprecated", "Select onDropdownVisibleChange deprecated", "Drawer width deprecated" or similar) to get the exact current replacement API for each. Check `frontend/package.json` for the exact antd version pinned so you're reading docs for the right version. Do not guess the replacement prop names — confirm them from docs, since a wrong swap could be a silent behavior change (e.g. antd v5 already renamed `onDropdownVisibleChange` to `onOpenChange`, but you must confirm v6's current recommendation, not assume v5's history carries over unchanged).
2. `grep -rn` `frontend/src` for each of `maskClosable`, `onDropdownVisibleChange`, and `Drawer` usages with a `width` prop, to find every call site (issue says "likely a small, mechanical, single-PR fix across a handful of components" — expect maybe 3-8 files total).
3. Create a branch `fix/issue-1275-antd-v6-deprecation-warnings` off `main`.
4. Swap each deprecated prop to its v6 replacement at every call site found. Preserve exact existing behavior — this is a prop rename/API migration, not a UX change. If a prop has no direct 1:1 replacement (e.g. it moved to a different config shape), read the antd docs carefully to replicate the same effective behavior, not just silence the warning.
5. Verify locally BEFORE committing: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` (or prettier --check, whichever this repo uses — check `frontend/package.json` scripts), `pnpm test` / `pnpm test:coverage`, and a TypeScript build check (`pnpm build` or `tsc --noEmit`, check package.json scripts). Then actually START the frontend dev server (check CLAUDE.md §8 quickstart / `docker-compose.yml` for how — may need the full stack, or just `pnpm dev` if the components render standalone) and use a browser (Playwright MCP tools are available: `mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_navigate`, `browser_console_messages`, etc.) to actually open a Modal, a Select dropdown, and the check-history Drawer, and confirm the three specific console warnings are GONE and nothing else broke. If starting the full authenticated stack is impractical in this environment (e.g. no seeded local DB/auth), do your best to at least verify via Storybook/component tests or a minimal reachable page, and clearly state in your report what you could and couldn't verify live in a browser — do not claim browser verification you didn't actually do.
6. Commit with a conventional commit message (`fix: ...` or `chore: ...`), body explaining the why, referencing the issue.
7. Push the branch and open a PR via `gh pr create` with `Fixes #1275` in the body. Use the repo's PR template if `.github/pull_request_template.md` exists.
8. Spawn the `/code-review` skill/slash-command flow on your own diff (mandatory per this repo's working agreements — never only an inline self-review); if unavailable, use the `pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer` agent type via the Agent tool against your diff. Fix anything it finds that's in scope.
9. Do NOT merge the PR — leave it open for CI + human merge.

In your final message: the PR URL, a one-line summary of every prop swapped and in which files, confirmation local verification (lint/format/test/build) passed, what you were and weren't able to verify live in a browser, and what code-review found (if anything).

title:	lineage: floor-denial message substitution is coupled to a string-equality literal, not structurally resilient
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	refactor
comments:	0
assignees:

Follow-up from the `/code-review` pass on #1305 (fixes #1264), deferred rather than fixed since it's a design trade-off within a deliberately narrow scope, not a bug.

`backend/app/lineage/warehouse_snowflake.py`, `SnowflakeLineageProvider.fetch_edges`, the branch handling OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES failing after a successful GET_LINEAGE traversal (~line 456, added in #1305):

```python
reason = _feature_unsupported_reason(exc)
if reason is not None:
    message = (
        _NOT_AUTHORIZED_OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES_MSG
        if reason == _NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG
        else reason
    )
    skipped.append(f"object_dependencies: {message}")
```

The substitution fires only while the shared classifier `_feature_unsupported_reason` returns the exact string literal `_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG`. If that function is later enriched (e.g. to append the denied object's name to the message), this `==` guard silently stops matching, the substitution never fires, and the misleading GET_LINEAGE-grant wording quietly comes back in this branch — with no test catching it, since the covering tests (`test_a_confirmed_floor_denial_after_a_successful_traversal_stays_prunable` and its already-partial sibling) assert only on the final rendered message under today's classifier, not on the coupling itself.

#1305 deliberately left `_feature_unsupported_reason` itself untouched/generic (it's shared across GET_LINEAGE, ACCESS_HISTORY, and this floor branch, and can't know which tier is calling it), so a same-PR fix would have widened scope beyond the two cosmetic findings in #1264. A structurally resilient version — e.g. `_feature_unsupported_reason` returning a small sentinel/enum distinguishing "confirmed denial, unspecified tier" from a tier-labelled variant, or accepting an optional tier-label parameter to interpolate into the message directly — would remove the string-equality coupling entirely.

Low priority — wording/robustness only, no behavioral defect today.

input.command:
gh issue create \
  --title "lineage: ACCESS_HISTORY not-authorized denial is also mislabeled with the GET_LINEAGE grant message" \
  --label "bug" \
  --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Sibling finding to #1264/#1305, surfaced by a review sub-agent while scoping that fix but never filed — flagging now so it doesn't fall through.

## What

`backend/app/lineage/warehouse_snowflake.py`, `_from_access_history` (~line 778): `except Exception as exc: _reraise_confirmed_or_transient(exc, "call failed")` routes through `_reraise_if_feature_unsupported` → `_feature_unsupported_reason(exc)` (~lines 1129–1150), which for any exception whose text contains `"does not exist or not authorized"` returns the literal, unparameterized `_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG` — "not authorized (role lacks the ACCOUNT_USAGE / GET_LINEAGE grant)" — naming the GET_LINEAGE grant regardless of which ACCOUNT_USAGE view actually failed.

Unlike the OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES branch in `fetch_edges` (fixed in #1305 for the after-successful-traversal case), the ACCESS_HISTORY branch has no message substitution: `_skip_reason` (~lines 1100–1102) returns `str(exc)` plus a transient suffix verbatim, and `fetch_edges`'s `except _FeatureUnsupportedError` handler (~lines 510–514) does `skipped.append(f"access_history: {_skip_reason(exc)}")` unchanged.

**Precondition correction vs. how this was first framed:** this is NOT "GET_LINEAGE succeeded but ACCESS_HISTORY's denial blames it anyway" — `fetch_edges` returns early whenever the GET_LINEAGE traversal (`top`) succeeds, so `_from_access_history` is only reached when GET_LINEAGE has *already* failed/skipped. The real shape is: GET_LINEAGE fails for any reason (possibly unrelated to grants), and ACCESS_HISTORY's *separate* not-authorized denial is *also* reported as a missing GET_LINEAGE grant — which is still wrong, since the file's own documented model (~lines 1157–1160) treats GET_LINEAGE, ACCESS_HISTORY, and OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES as gated by distinct grants.

## Evidence

No test asserts the ACCESS_HISTORY-specific wording is correct: `test_not_authorized_tier_descends_instead_of_aborting` only asserts the substring `"not authorized"` is present and raw `"002003"` text is absent — it never asserts the tier name is right, and in that test GET_LINEAGE is *also* denied so the wrong grant name happens to look plausible. No test exercises GET_LINEAGE failing for a non-grant reason simultaneously with ACCESS_HISTORY failing not-authorized, which would make the mislabeling obvious.

## Suggested direction

Same shape as #1305's fix: give the ACCESS_HISTORY branch its own message (naming ACCESS_HISTORY specifically) instead of reusing `_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG` verbatim. #1307 (filed alongside #1305) proposes a more structural fix — a sentinel/enum or tier-label parameter on `_feature_unsupported_reason` — which would cover this site too and avoid a third near-identical string-substitution branch if tackled together.

Low priority — cosmetic/wording, not a behavioral or security issue; an operator reading the message would investigate the wrong grant.
EOF
)" 2>&1

**One tangentially relevant note, from #1121's code review** (CheckEdit trend Drawer PR): the reviewer flagged that an inline code comment claiming a component "never loads until the drawer is actually opened" (referring to recharts) was **false** — it was a static import that loads with the route chunk, not lazily on drawer-open. No prior concerns exist about `width`→`size` on either Drawer (CheckEdit trend drawer, App.tsx mobile nav drawer) or about `mask.closable` semantics — this appears to be a genuinely low-risk, previously-undiscussed area of the codebase.</result>

I reviewed the full history of all four files (`git log -p`, targeted `git log -S<prop>`, and the commits that introduced each line). Summary per concern area requested:

**1. `maskClosable={false}` in `ProfileCompletionPrompt.tsx` — no concern.**
Introduced in PR #1153 (`27779d14`, the first-login profile-completion feature). The docstring explains the intent clearly: dismissing the modal by mask-click, Esc, or the X are all treated identically as "skip" (routed through the same `dismiss()` handler bound to `onCancel`). `maskClosable={false}` only blocks the mask-click path from closing without going through `onCancel` — but `onCancel` still fires via Esc/X, so `dismiss()` still runs either way. `mask={{ closable: false }}` is antd v6's documented 1:1 replacement and preserves this exactly. Corroborating evidence: `ApiKeysPanel.tsx` (PR #636, `181993c6`, predates this PR) already uses `mask={{ closable: !created }}` for an analogous "force explicit acknowledge" case — so this exact replacement shape is proven, working prior art in this codebase, not a guess.

**2. `onDropdownVisibleChange` → `onOpenChange` in `SamplePolicyPanel.tsx` — no concern, but worth noting the load-bearing behavior it must preserve.**
Introduced in PR #635/#641 (`a9e2b27e`). The PR history shows this callback backs a **lazy, fetch-once column introspection**: `loadColumns()` fires on dropdown open and a follow-up review-driven commit (same PR) explicitly hardened "introspects at most once across repeated dropdown opens" as load-bearing behavior, plus graceful degradation to free-tag entry if the fetch fails. Since `onOpenChange` is antd's direct rename with an identical `(open: boolean) => void` signature and identical firing point, the fetch-once guard (which lives inside `loadColumns`/the async-data hook, not in the prop itself) is unaffected. The existing test file (`frontend/tests/components/SamplePolicyPanel.test.tsx`) drives this via real `userEvent.click` on the combobox rather than asserting the prop name, so it will validate the swap transparently. No pre-existing `onOpenChange` usage elsewhere in the codebase conflicts with this.

**3. `width={520}` → `size={520}` in `CheckEdit.tsx` (trend drawer) — no concern.**
This Drawer was added recently in PR #1121 (`f7047424`, 2026-08-01, the metric-trend-view feature) with no special history around the `width` value itself — it's just a fixed drawer width, no prior bug or comment attached to it.

**4. `width={SHELL.siderWidth}` → `size={...}` in `App.tsx` (mobile nav drawer) — no concern.**
Added in PR #801/#817 (`e3cdf11a`, the narrow-viewport overlay-nav fix). `SHELL.siderWidth` is used so the overlay Drawer matches the desktop Sider's width — purely a visual-consistency constant, not tied to any behavioral bug.

**Notable corroborating context (not a concern, but useful): this Drawer `width`→`size` migration already happened once, codebase-wide.**
PR #516 (`79d4aa83`, 2026-07-01, "refactor(frontend): migrate off deprecated antd v6 APIs") already renamed every `Drawer width` to `size` across ~15 files, and its commit message explicitly notes "Modal `width` is NOT deprecated — left as-is" (consistent with PR #1308 not touching any Modal `width`). The two `width` instances PR #1308 now fixes in `App.tsx` and `CheckEdit.tsx` are **new code written after PR #516 landed** (`e3cdf11a` on a later date, `f7047424` on 2026-08-01) — i.e., they're regressions of an already-fixed pattern that crept back in because nothing (lint rule/CI check) enforces it going forward. This isn't a defect in PR #1308 itself, but it suggests the DataQ team might want a lint rule or periodic sweep to catch future antd deprecated-prop reintroductions rather than relying on manual QA passes (as happened via #1275) to catch them again.

**Overall: no historical bug, PR discussion, or comment found that contradicts the intent of any of the four prop swaps in PR #1308. All four are faithful 1:1 replacements per the commit's own stated verification, and none of the four lines carry hidden intent that the antd v6 replacement would break.**</result>

Both review threads for #1266 have now converged on the same two real bugs (not nits) — cross-confirmed by independent passes:

1. **Driver misclassification**: `drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg")` returns `False` for a bare `postgresql://` URL, but SQLAlchemy actually resolves that to psycopg2 by default (verified live). So the *most common* `DATABASE_URL` shape gets its `connect_timeout`/`keepalives` protections silently dropped — reintroducing the exact stale-connection hangs (#1102/#1221) the guard exists to prevent. The new unit test currently locks in this wrong behavior as "correct."
2. **The `options` (lock_timeout) key was left unconditional**, with a comment claiming it's "portable across drivers" — untrue for asyncpg/pg8000, whose `connect()` has no `options` parameter. So a genuinely non-psycopg driver would still crash with the same `TypeError` at first connect that #1266 was meant to eliminate.

Both are legitimate correctness bugs in the fix itself, not scope creep. Waiting for the agent to correct them before it opens the PR — I'll report back once it lands.

+"""Shared driver guard for psycopg-only `connect_args` keys (#1266).
+
+`connect_timeout` and the `keepalives*` family (`keepalives`, `keepalives_idle`,
+`keepalives_interval`, `keepalives_count`) are libpq connection parameters, not
+portable SQLAlchemy `connect_args` — the psycopg2 and psycopg (psycopg3) drivers
+both pass them straight through to libpq, but any other driver's `connect()`
+raises `TypeError` on the unrecognized kwarg. That raise happens at the FIRST REAL
+CONNECTION ATTEMPT, not at `create_engine()`/`engine_from_config()` call time — so
+it would surface as an opaque crash deep in app/worker/migrate-job startup, not a
+clear config error.
+
+`Settings.database_url` has no scheme/driver validator and is env-overridable via
+`DATABASE_URL`, so both real engine-building call sites —
+`backend/app/db/session.py`'s `_build_engine()` and `backend/alembic/env.py`'s
+`run_migrations_online()` — need this guard, not just one of them. This mirrors
+the driver check `backend/tests/conftest.py`'s `_probe_postgres` already uses for
+the identical reason (guarding its own, narrower, `connect_timeout`-only probe).
+"""
+
+from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url
+
+
+def psycopg_connect_args(database_url: str, **driver_only_args: object) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Return `driver_only_args` unchanged when `database_url` resolves to a
+    psycopg-family SQLAlchemy driver (`postgresql+psycopg2` or the psycopg3
+    `postgresql+psycopg`), else `{}`.
+
+    A non-psycopg driver then degrades to no keepalives/connect_timeout instead of
+    `create_engine()`/`engine_from_config()` raising `TypeError` on the first real
+    connection attempt.
+    """
+    try:
+        is_psycopg = make_url(database_url).drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg")
+    except Exception:
+        # An unparseable URL isn't this guard's story to tell — `create_engine`
+        # itself raises on it soon enough, with a clearer error than we'd add here.
+        is_psycopg = False
+    return dict(driver_only_args) if is_psycopg else {}

Verify locally: Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit, and `pytest backend/tests/db/` (plus anything else touching `_build_engine`/`run_migrations_online`, e.g. `backend/tests/services/test_poll_lock_timeout.py` — check it still passes given it depends on ambient `DATABASE_URL` resolving to psycopg-family per a prior review note, should be unaffected by your fix but confirm).

  --title "frontend: no lint guard against reintroducing deprecated antd v6 props" \
  --label "chore" \
  --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Surfaced by a review pass on #1308 (fixes #1275) while tracing git history on the touched files, not itself a defect in that PR — filed as its own follow-up per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a.

## What

PR #516 (2026-07-01, "refactor(frontend): migrate off deprecated antd v6 APIs") already did a codebase-wide sweep renaming every `Drawer width` to `size` (~15 files) plus other deprecated-prop cleanup, specifically to silence antd v6 console deprecation warnings.

#1275/#1308 (2026-08-12) found and fixed three deprecation warnings again — `Modal.maskClosable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`, and (again) `Drawer.width` — and #1308's own git-history review confirmed the two `Drawer.width` sites it touched (`App.tsx`'s mobile nav drawer, `CheckEdit.tsx`'s trend drawer) were **written after PR #516 landed**, i.e. genuine regressions of an already-fixed pattern, not something #516 missed.

## Why it recurred

Nothing enforces the deprecated-prop migration going forward — it's caught only by manual QA passes (as happened via the #1275 issue, "found during a full real-user QA pass") rather than at commit/CI time. ESLint doesn't flag deprecated antd props by default.

## Suggested direction

- Check whether `eslint-plugin-react` or an antd-specific lint plugin can flag deprecated prop usage (antd ships `@ant-design/codemod-v5`-style tooling for major-version migrations; check if v6 has an equivalent, or if TypeScript's own `@deprecated` JSDoc tags on antd's prop types already surface as editor/IDE warnings that could be promoted to a CI-enforced `tsc`/ESLint error, e.g. via `eslint-plugin-deprecation` or `@typescript-eslint`'s `no-deprecated` rule if available for this ESLint/TS version).
- Alternative if no clean lint rule exists: a periodic grep-based CI check (or a pre-commit hook) for the known-deprecated prop names as a stopgap, documented as "extend this list on future antd major bumps."

Low priority — cosmetic console noise, not a functional defect, and the fix is cheap when caught by QA. But it's the second time this exact category has recurred, so worth a small structural fix before a third occurrence.
EOF

"""Shared driver guard for psycopg-only `connect_args` keys (#1266).

`connect_timeout` and the `keepalives*` family (`keepalives`, `keepalives_idle`,
`keepalives_interval`, `keepalives_count`) are libpq connection parameters, not
portable SQLAlchemy `connect_args` — the psycopg2 and psycopg (psycopg3) drivers
both pass them straight through to libpq, but any other driver's `connect()`
raises `TypeError` on the unrecognized kwarg. That raise happens at the FIRST REAL
CONNECTION ATTEMPT, not at `create_engine()`/`engine_from_config()` call time — so
it would surface as an opaque crash deep in app/worker/migrate-job startup, not a
clear config error.

`Settings.database_url` has no scheme/driver validator and is env-overridable via
`DATABASE_URL`, so both real engine-building call sites —
`backend/app/db/session.py`'s `_build_engine()` and `backend/alembic/env.py`'s
`run_migrations_online()` — need this guard, not just one of them. This mirrors
the driver check `backend/tests/conftest.py`'s `_probe_postgres` already uses for
the identical reason (guarding its own, narrower, `connect_timeout`-only probe).
"""

from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url

_PSYCOPG_FAMILY_DRIVERS = frozenset({"psycopg2", "psycopg"})


def psycopg_connect_args(database_url: str, **driver_only_args: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return `driver_only_args` unchanged when `database_url` resolves to a
    psycopg-family SQLAlchemy driver (`postgresql+psycopg2` or the psycopg3
    `postgresql+psycopg`), else `{}`.

    A non-psycopg driver then degrades to no keepalives/connect_timeout instead of
    `create_engine()`/`engine_from_config()` raising `TypeError` on the first real
    connection attempt.

    Classifies by the DRIVER SQLAlchemy will actually instantiate
    (`URL.get_dialect().driver`), not by a string-prefix match on `drivername`. A
    prefix check on `drivername` returns `False` for a bare `postgresql://` URL — but
    SQLAlchemy resolves a bare `postgresql://` scheme to the psycopg2 dialect BY
    DEFAULT, so a prefix check silently drops these libpq params (and, historically,
    reintroduces #1102/#1221) for the single most common `DATABASE_URL` shape.
    `get_dialect()` only imports SQLAlchemy's own dialect wrapper class — it does not
    require the underlying DBAPI package (`psycopg2`/`asyncpg`/`pg8000`/…) to be
    installed, so this works standalone for a driver this environment has never
    imported.
    """
    try:
        is_psycopg = make_url(database_url).get_dialect().driver in _PSYCOPG_FAMILY_DRIVERS
    except Exception:
        # An unparseable URL, or a driver name SQLAlchemy has no dialect plugin for,
        # isn't this guard's story to tell — `create_engine` itself raises on it soon
        # enough, with a clearer error than we'd add here.
        is_psycopg = False
    return dict(driver_only_args) if is_psycopg else {}

title:	Deep offset paging on /runs, /pipeline_runs, /incidents has no supporting (created_at, id) index
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	enhancement, priority/P3
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	1245
--
## Context

#1108 (PR #1231) gave `/runs`, `/pipeline_runs` and `/incidents` an `X-Total-Count` header and, for `/runs`, `offset` paging plus a total-order `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` tie-break. All three list endpoints now page the same way:

| endpoint | table | order | max `limit` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /runs` | `runs` | `created_at DESC, id DESC` | 200 |
| `GET /pipeline_runs` | `pipeline_runs` | `created_at DESC, id DESC` | 200 |
| `GET /incidents` | `incidents` | `created_at DESC, id DESC` | 500 |

**None of the three tables has an index that matches that ordering.** Today they carry only single-column indexes:

- `runs` — `ix_runs_suite_id`, `ix_runs_status`, `ix_runs_asset_id`, plus the composite `ix_runs_suite_created` on `(suite_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)`
- `pipeline_runs` — `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline`, `ix_pipeline_runs_connection_id`
- `incidents` — `ix_incidents_asset_id`, `ix_incidents_check_id`, `ix_incidents_suite_id`, `ix_incidents_status`

`ix_runs_suite_created` covers the *suite-scoped* read (`?suite_id=`) and the `datasource_health` LATERAL from #999. It does **not** cover the unfiltered list, which is `suite_id IN (<every accessible suite>)` — the default Results-page read and the whole workspace-admin view. That plan is a full scan + sort, and `OFFSET` makes it worse linearly: the database materialises and discards every skipped row on every page.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed in #1231

- The gap is **identical on all three tables**, and is pre-existing on two of them (`pipeline_runs` since #928, `incidents` since #772). Adding an ad-hoc index to `runs` alone inside a header-shaped PR would be an arbitrary partial fix.
- Index choice here wants **EXPLAIN evidence at real row counts**, not a guess. Prod's `runs`/`incidents` tables are currently small enough that the planner may prefer a seq scan regardless, so an index added now could be dead weight that only costs write amplification.
- This is purely a performance concern — **no correctness or honesty defect**. The totals and the paging are correct today; they are just not cheap at depth.

It belongs with the "v1.1 W6 scale-aware execution" work, which is where the row-count growth assumptions get made.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Capture `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for each of the three list queries at a realistic row count (seeded, or prod if the volume is there) — both the unfiltered read and the common filtered ones (`?suite_id=`, `?status=`, `?provider=`, `?state=`).
- [ ] Decide per table whether a `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` composite (or a filter-leading variant such as `(status, created_at DESC, id DESC)`) actually changes the plan. **Record the evidence, including a decision not to add one** — a measured "the planner ignores it at our volume" is a valid and useful outcome.
- [ ] If added: an additive index-only migration (no data change, no column change), tested up **and** down locally, with the model `__table_args__` kept in sync.
- [ ] Consider whether `OFFSET` should give way to keyset/seek paging on the deepest surface — the ordering is already total, which is the precondition for it.

## Not in scope

Changing the response contract. `X-Total-Count` and the current `limit`/`offset` parameters stay as #1108 shipped them.

Follow-up from the `/code-review` pass on PR #1231 (finding 2).

title:	alerting: centralize the already-logged-traceback downgrade in the structlog processor chain, not per-caller
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	refactor
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	1261
--
Follow-up from the `/code-review` pass on #1260 (fixes #1226). Deferred out of that PR because the fix there is small, narrow (2 call sites), fully tested, and matches an existing codebase precedent (`_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR` in `backend/app/worker/celery_app.py`) — not a bug, an architectural preference worth recording rather than acting on immediately.

## What

#1226 fixed a real bug: when every alert channel fails, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` (`backend/app/alerting/composite.py`) logs a full traceback per failing channel before re-raising the last one, and both callers (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) then logged that SAME last-channel traceback a second time. The fix adds `mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` (`backend/app/alerting/base.py`) — a plain attribute the composite sets on the re-raised exception — and each caller's `except Exception:` block checks it to downgrade to `log.warning` instead of `log.exception`.

## The concern

The downgrade decision (`if was_already_logged(exc): log.warning(...) else: log.exception(...)`) is duplicated verbatim in `dispatch.py` and `main.py`, and is **opt-in per caller** — a future consumer of `publish_health`/`publish_poll_staleness` (e.g. a new orchestration-health path) that forgets the check silently reintroduces the exact double-traceback bug #1226 fixes, with nothing (no test, no lint rule) to catch the omission.

CLAUDE.md §10 and the `feedback_redact_at_the_logger_not_the_call_site` precedent (PR #849) establish the pattern for this class of problem: **PII redaction happens once, centrally, in `backend/app/core/logging.py`'s processor chain — not at every call site.** The same shape could apply here: a shared structlog processor already has access to `exc_info` (and therefore the exception object, since `exc_info` is `(type, value, tb)`) and could check `was_already_logged` there, downgrading the level for ANY caller automatically, not just the two that currently remember to ask.

## Why not done in #1260

- Only 2 call sites exist today, not 3+ — the cost/benefit of a processor-chain abstraction is weaker than #1101's "copy-pasted loop" precedent that justified extracting `_fan_out_delivered_first" itself.
- The processor-chain approach needs care: unlike PII redaction (which only ever REMOVES data), silently downgrading a log LEVEL based on an exception attribute is a bigger behavioral change to make globally — worth its own design pass, not a drive-by extraction.

## Suggested direction

Add a structlog processor (alongside `_redact_pii` in `backend/app/core/logging.py`) that inspects `event_dict.get("exc_info")`, extracts the exception instance, and if `was_already_logged(exc)` is true, rewrites the event's level from error to warning and drops `exc_info`. Then remove the per-caller checks in `dispatch.py`/`main.py` — they become unconditional `log.exception(...)` again, with the processor doing the actual downgrade.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A third (or later) caller of the composite's delivered-first methods gets the downgrade automatically, with no per-caller opt-in.
- [ ] The two existing call sites simplify back to unconditional `log.exception(...)`.
- [ ] Existing #1226 regression tests (asserting `log_level`/`exc_info` via `capture_logs`) still pass, proving the observable behavior is unchanged.

title:	core_table: 3-part (catalog) names don't quote the catalog or schema — #476 fix is table/column-only
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	936
--
Found by the agentic review of the #476 casing fix (PR on `fix/issue-476-monitor-identifier-quoting`). Filed rather than fixed in-PR because the correct fix needs dialect awareness the builder deliberately doesn't have.

## Problem

`backend/app/datasources/sql.py` `core_table` builds a 3-part `catalog.schema.table` namespace as a single unquoted `quoted_name`:

```python
namespace = quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)
```

`quote=False` means "never quote this string" — which is required so the dialect emits three dotted parts instead of quoting the whole dotted string as one identifier. But it suppresses quoting for the **catalog and schema** too, not just the dots.

So the #476 casing fix only reaches the table and column in the 3-part form:

```
table=Orders schema=Retail catalog=MyCat
  ->  SELECT count(*) FROM MyCat.Retail."Orders"     (Snowflake)
```

A schema created as `"Retail"` is stored mixed-case and only reachable quoted; emitted bare it folds to `RETAIL` and fails — exactly the bug #476 fixed for columns.

## Blast radius today: nil

- Unity Catalog is the only caller that passes a `catalog` (`unity_catalog.py`), and Databricks resolves identifiers case-insensitively, so the missing quotes are harmless there.
- Snowflake passes `catalog=None`, so it never takes this path.

|---|---|---|---|

| `GET /pipeline_runs` | `pipeline_runs` | `created_at DESC, id DESC` | 200 |
| `GET /incidents` | `incidents` | `created_at DESC, id DESC` | 500 |

**None of the three tables has an index that matches that ordering.** Today they carry only single-column indexes:

- `runs` — `ix_runs_suite_id`, `ix_runs_status`, `ix_runs_asset_id`, plus the composite `ix_runs_suite_created` on `(suite_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)`
- `pipeline_runs` — `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline`, `ix_pipeline_runs_connection_id`
- `incidents` — `ix_incidents_asset_id`, `ix_incidents_check_id`, `ix_incidents_suite_id`, `ix_incidents_status`

`ix_runs_suite_created` covers the *suite-scoped* read (`?suite_id=`) and the `datasource_health` LATERAL from #999. It does **not** cover the unfiltered list, which is `suite_id IN (<every accessible suite>)` — the default Results-page read and the whole workspace-admin view. That plan is a full scan + sort, and `OFFSET` makes it worse linearly: the database materialises and discards every skipped row on every page.

Follow-up from the `/code-review` pass on #1260 (fixes #1226). Deferred out of that PR because the fix there is small, narrow (2 call sites), fully tested, and matches an existing codebase precedent (`_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR` in `backend/app/worker/celery_app.py`) — not a bug, an architectural preference worth recording rather than acting on immediately.

## What

#1226 fixed a real bug: when every alert channel fails, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` (`backend/app/alerting/composite.py`) logs a full traceback per failing channel before re-raising the last one, and both callers (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) then logged that SAME last-channel traceback a second time. The fix adds `mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` (`backend/app/alerting/base.py`) — a plain attribute the composite sets on the re-raised exception — and each caller's `except Exception:` block checks it to downgrade to `log.warning` instead of `log.exception`.

## The concern

The downgrade decision (`if was_already_logged(exc): log.warning(...) else: log.exception(...)`) is duplicated verbatim in `dispatch.py` and `main.py`, and is **opt-in per caller** — a future consumer of `publish_health`/`publish_poll_staleness` (e.g. a new orchestration-health path) that forgets the check silently reintroduces the exact double-traceback bug #1226 fixes, with nothing (no test, no lint rule) to catch the omission.

CLAUDE.md §10 and the `feedback_redact_at_the_logger_not_the_call_site` precedent (PR #849) establish the pattern for this class of problem: **PII redaction happens once, centrally, in `backend/app/core/logging.py`'s processor chain — not at every call site.** The same shape could apply here: a shared structlog processor already has access to `exc_info` (and therefore the exception object, since `exc_info` is `(type, value, tb)`) and could check `was_already_logged` there, downgrading the level for ANY caller automatically, not just the two that currently remember to ask.

## Why not done in #1260

- Only 2 call sites exist today, not 3+ — the cost/benefit of a processor-chain abstraction is weaker than #1101's "copy-pasted loop" precedent that justified extracting `_fan_out_delivered_first" itself.
- The processor-chain approach needs care: unlike PII redaction (which only ever REMOVES data), silently downgrading a log LEVEL based on an exception attribute is a bigger behavioral change to make globally — worth its own design pass, not a drive-by extraction.

## Suggested direction

Add a structlog processor (alongside `_redact_pii` in `backend/app/core/logging.py`) that inspects `event_dict.get("exc_info")`, extracts the exception instance, and if `was_already_logged(exc)` is true, rewrites the event's level from error to warning and drops `exc_info`. Then remove the per-caller checks in `dispatch.py`/`main.py` — they become unconditional `log.exception(...)` again, with the processor doing the actual downgrade.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A third (or later) caller of the composite's delivered-first methods gets the downgrade automatically, with no per-caller opt-in.
- [ ] The two existing call sites simplify back to unconditional `log.exception(...)`.
- [ ] Existing #1226 regression tests (asserting `log_level`/`exc_info` via `capture_logs`) still pass, proving the observable behavior is unchanged.

Filed from the `/code-review` pass on PR #1233 (batch-target preview, #1193). Deferred out of that PR because the fix is a design change (bounds + cancellation), not a line edit, and the endpoint is authenticated + edit-gated + rate-limited, so this is a hardening gap rather than an open door.

## What

`GET /api/v1/suites/{id}/batch-preview` (`preview_batch_target` in `backend/app/api/v1/suites.py`, service `run_target.preview_batch`) is a **sync** endpoint that does a **live object listing** under the caller's prefix and matches a **caller-supplied regex** against every key. Two consequences:

1. **Thread-pool pressure.** Sync endpoints run in Starlette's bounded threadpool (40 threads by default). The listing is bounded only by `flatfile._BATCH_LISTING_MAX` (500,000 objects) with no wall-clock timeout and no cancellation. The frontend `BatchPreviewHint` auto-fires it on form mount and on every 400 ms typing pause, and it does not `AbortController`-cancel a superseded request (it only ignores the result). One author on a broad prefix can therefore hold several threads for a long time and stall every other sync endpoint in the API.

   This differs from the run path, where the same listing happens **in the Celery worker**, and from the dry-run/profiler endpoints, which are bounded by the datasource's own query timeout rather than by an object count.

2. **ReDoS surface moved into the API.** `run_target.resolve_target` already `re.compile`s a user pattern in the API process at save time, but *matching* it against arbitrary keys previously only ever happened in the worker. This endpoint is the first place the API process runs a user regex over attacker-influenceable input (object key names), so a catastrophic-backtracking pattern now pins an API thread instead of a worker.

## Suggested direction

- A wall-clock/object budget for the *preview* specifically, well below `_BATCH_LISTING_MAX` — a preview does not need to be exhaustive to be useful, and "scanned the first N and found no match" is an honest answer we can render (the honesty bar #1105 set for asset truncation).
- Client-side `AbortController` on supersession in `BatchPreviewHint`, so a fast typist doesn't leave N in-flight listings behind.
- Consider moving the preview off the sync path (or onto the worker) if the budget can't be made tight enough.
- Bound the regex work — a length cap on the pattern, and/or a per-key match budget.

## Acceptance

- A preview against a very large prefix returns within a bounded time with an honest partial answer, and cannot hold an API thread indefinitely.
- Superseded preview requests are cancelled client-side, not merely ignored.
- A pathological backtracking pattern cannot pin an API worker thread.

def folding_identifier(name: str) -> Any:
    """Wrap ``name`` with an explicit quote decision: bare iff it is all lower-case.

    The #476 rule, made ours instead of SQLAlchemy's. Left to its defaults the
    compiler also quotes any name in the **dialect's reserved-word set**, which is
    not the same set the warehouse reserves — Snowflake does not reserve ``copy``,
    but SQLAlchemy's Snowflake dialect does, so a column stored ``COPY`` (created
    unquoted as ``copy``) would be emitted as ``"copy"`` and stop resolving. That
    is the very failure #476 exists to remove, reintroduced for one word.

    Pinning the decision explicitly makes the emitted form depend only on case:

    * **all lower-case → never quoted**, so the warehouse folds it exactly as it
      did before #476 (``order_ts`` → ``ORDER_TS``). This is what makes the change
      byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving rather than approximately so.
    * **anything else → always quoted**, which is the whole point: a mixed-case
      column is only reachable quoted.

    Genuinely reserved words (``order``, ``select``) are unreachable either way —
    bare is a parse error, and the folded object is ``ORDER``, which ``"order"``
    does not match. They were broken before this change and are broken after it,
    identically; alias them in a view.
    """
    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name

    return quoted_name(name, quote=name != name.lower())


def core_table(*, table: str, schema: str | None, catalog: str | None) -> TableClause:
    """A Core table clause for ``[catalog.][schema.]table`` — the dialect quotes it.

    The one construction shared by the profiler's query builders and the monitor
    engine (#476). Going through Core rather than f-string interpolation is what
    makes a **mixed-case identifier** work at all, per `folding_identifier`'s rule.

    It must be Core and not hand-rolled quoting because the quote character is
    **dialect-specific** — Snowflake uses ``"``, Databricks/Unity Catalog uses
    backticks and reads ``"..."`` as a string literal — and this module is shared
    by both.

    **Known limit — the 3-part (catalog) form does not get the #476 treatment.**
    Core's ``schema=`` slot is a single string, so a ``catalog.schema`` namespace
    has to be passed as one *unquoted* ``quoted_name`` for the dialect to emit
    dotted parts rather than quoting the whole thing as one identifier. That
    suppresses quoting for the catalog and schema too, so a mixed-case *catalog or
    schema* still folds. Only the table and column are quote-correct here.

    Building the namespace from pre-quoted parts would mean choosing the quote
    character ourselves, which is exactly the dialect-specific mistake this
    function exists to avoid — so the limit is recorded rather than papered over.
    It is currently unreachable: Unity Catalog is the only caller that passes a
    catalog and resolves identifiers case-insensitively, and Snowflake passes
    ``catalog=None``. Tracked as #936; pinned by a test so it reads as a recorded
    limitation rather than a guarantee.

    That unquoted namespace is also the one raw interpolation left in the module,
    hence the allowlist check on every part here rather than trusting callers
    (they validate first for a good error message; this is the injection
    guarantee, and it survives a caller forgetting to validate).

    A ``catalog`` with no ``schema`` is refused: dropping the ``None`` schema would
    emit a 2-part ``catalog.table``, which Unity Catalog resolves as
    ``schema.table`` — a wrong object rather than an error.
    """
    from sqlalchemy import table as table_clause
    from sqlalchemy.sql import quoted_name

    if catalog is not None and schema is None:
        raise ValueError(f"table {table!r} has a catalog but no schema")
    for part, label in ((table, "table"), (schema, "schema"), (catalog, "catalog")):
        if part is not None and not is_sql_identifier(part):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid {label} identifier: {part!r}")

    namespace: Any = None if schema is None else folding_identifier(schema)
    if catalog is not None:
        namespace = quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)
    return table_clause(folding_identifier(table), schema=namespace)


class LazyEngine:
    """One lazily-built SQLAlchemy engine with an idempotent dispose (#427).

    ``factory`` builds the engine on first :meth:`get` (the runner's URL /
    connect-args closure — the only per-datasource variance); every later call
    returns the same engine, so a runner's SQL touchpoints share one pool and
    one auth handshake per run. :meth:`close` disposes the pool and resets, so
    a closed holder lazily rebuilds if reused — never a bricked runner.
    """

title:	lineage: a suspended snapshot prune has no durable, product-visible backstop — it can stay suspended indefinitely
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	1236
--
Found by the `/code-review` pass on #1220 and deliberately deferred there (it needs a persisted marker, i.e. a migration, which #1220 explicitly has none of).

## What

#1220 introduced `WarehouseLineageResult.prunable`: a snapshot pull that only PARTIALLY observed current state (a tier skipped or half-traversed for a transient reason) is persisted accrete-only, with no stale-edge prune. Its module docstring promises:

> The next clean pull prunes normally, so a genuinely removed dependency is at worst one cycle late — the cheap side of the trade.

**Nothing enforces that a clean pull ever arrives.** Any *persistent* condition that reads as transient — a statement timeout on call 1 every cycle, a driver-shape error that `_feature_unsupported_reason`'s two narrow patterns don't match — leaves `authoritative_snapshot` False on every refresh, and `lineage_edges` accretes indefinitely with no prune. The promise degrades from "one cycle late" to "never", silently.

(The likeliest concrete path — a confirmed per-object denial recurring every cycle — was closed inside #1220 itself: only UNCLASSIFIED failures set `prunable=False`. What is left is the genuinely-unclassifiable-but-persistent case.)

## Current mitigation, and why it is not enough

#1220 emits `warehouse_lineage_prune_suspended` at WARNING on every suspended cycle, so the condition is alertable in App Insights, and `lineage_degraded_reason` carries the transient tag on the connection. But:

- `WarehouseRefreshOutcome` does not carry the suspension, so no API/UI surface can report it.
- Nothing records **how long** it has been suspended — an operator cannot distinguish "blipped once last night" from "has not pruned in three weeks", which is precisely the #828/#1091 class of blindness (a real problem the product reports as merely 'degraded').

## Options (pick at design time)

1. **Bounded suspension.** Persist `lineage_last_authoritative_refresh_at`; once it is older than `LINEAGE_STALE_AFTER_HOURS` (already defined, default 48h), prune anyway on the next successful pull — a stale-but-honest graph beats an unboundedly accreting one. Needs one nullable timestamp column.
2. **Report it.** Plumb the suspension (and its age) through `WarehouseRefreshOutcome` → connection state → `warehouse_lineage_status`, so the existing lineage banner says "pruning suspended since X".

(1) and (2) are complementary; (2) alone is the honest-degradation minimum, (1) is the self-healing one.

## AC

- [ ] A snapshot connection whose prune has been suspended for longer than the configured threshold is either pruned anyway or visibly reported as suspended (with an age) on a product surface, not only in logs
- [ ] The choice is recorded in `warehouse_refresh`'s module docstring, which currently states the unenforced "at worst one cycle late" promise
- [ ] Test covering N consecutive partial cycles, asserting the backstop fires

title:	docs: marketplace-listing readiness checklist — free OSS + BYOL (license audit clear; prerequisites & good-to-haves)
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	documentation, enhancement, priority/P2
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	DataQ Roadmap (Todo)
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog

--
Documentation/tracking record of the 2026-07-09 marketplace-listing readiness review, updated for the **distribution model chosen 2026-07-09: free open-source software + customer-deployed BYOL** (refines ADR 0013 — the "licensing model + entitlement/license-key" line in §5 is superseded by this choice; no license-key/entitlement machinery is needed when the license is the OSS grant itself).

## License audit result (2026-07-09): free OSS + BYOL is CLEAR — no contradictions

- **Project license:** MIT (`LICENSE`, © 2026 Arijit Roy) — ideal for free OSS + BYOL; marketplaces support free/BYOL container offers of OSS.
- **Backend (full conda env, 239 packages):** **zero strong copyleft / source-available licenses.** Key deps confirmed from installed metadata: great-expectations 1.17.2 (Apache-2.0), fastmcp (Apache-2.0), fastapi/sqlalchemy/pydantic/alembic (MIT), celery/uvicorn/pandas/numpy (BSD), snowflake + databricks connectors, boto3, pyiceberg, pyarrow, opentelemetry (Apache-2.0), `caio` (Apache-2.0, verified via bundled COPYING). Weak copyleft only: `psycopg2-binary` (LGPL-3.0, dynamically linked — fine to ship, include notice), `certifi`/`pathspec` (MPL-2.0, file-level).
- **Frontend (node_modules sweep, 643 packages):** **zero strong copyleft.** MIT 526 / Apache-2.0 42 / ISC 33 / BSD 18. Weak copyleft: `lightningcss` (MPL-2.0, build-time only — not distributed), `dompurify` (dual MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 — take Apache). `@fontsource/*` fonts are OFL-1.1 (standard for bundling web fonts). The UNKNOWN-license hits are nested test fixtures inside deps, not in the lockfile — not shipped.
- **Net obligations when distributing images/bundles:** preserve upstream copyright/license notices (MIT/BSD) and Apache-2.0 NOTICE content → ship a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES file (or SBOM with license data) in images and releases. That's the whole compliance surface.

## Prerequisites (blocking a listing)

**Decision & legal**
- [ ] Amend/append ADR recording the free-OSS + BYOL distribution decision (supersedes ADR 0013 §5's entitlement/license-key line; keep MIT) — **in progress: ADR 0031, PR #733**
- [ ] THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES (or SPDX SBOM) generated and shipped in images + GitHub releases; wire generation into CI/publish
- [ ] **G-h:** paid Databricks workspace before any commercial demo/use (Free Edition is non-commercial-only; decision of 2026-07-03 stands — trigger is exactly a listing)
- [ ] Marketplace seller registration + per-marketplace review (Partner Center for Azure Phase 1); note free offers still go through certification
- [ ] **Listing terms / EULA:** attach license terms in Partner Center — required even for $0 offers (Standard Contract or MIT-based custom terms). *(ADR 0013 §5 survivor — a free offer does not waive this.)*
- [ ] **SOC 2 / pen test posture decided:** enterprise-procurement ask independent of price (ADR 0013 §5 survivor). Decide defer-until-demand vs pre-emptive, and record the decision — don't leave it unowned.
- [ ] **DPA:** *not needed* while there is no hosted/paid service — self-hosted BYOL creates no data-processor relationship. Recorded here as a conscious disposition (ADR 0013 §5 survivor); revisit the day a hosted tier exists.
- [ ] **Tax/banking (Partner Center payout profile):** *not needed* for a free offer — recorded as a conscious disposition (ADR 0013 §5 survivor); required the day any paid offer/tier ships (ADR 0031 Decision 5 keeps that door open).
- [ ] Support expectations stated: SUPPORT.md (community support channels for free OSS; SLA only if a paid tier ever appears)
- [ ] Privacy posture stated: a short statement that DataQ is self-hosted and phones nothing home (verifiably true today — keep it that way)

**Product hygiene (G-i teardown)**
- [ ] G-i deployed-side teardown before any distributable artifact: strip Flows A/B/C, the 5 harness connections, demo suites/users, seeded-breach check from the reference deployment (checklist already in deploy/README.md)
- [ ] #730 — repo-side G-i slice: remove the real prod FQDN from tracked files (backend test, deploy/README, CLAUDE.md)
- [ ] #729 — fix stale SECURITY.md "no versioned releases" claim
- [ ] Split eval vs install paths: `docker-compose.ghcr.yml` always seeds demo data and forces auth-bypass — fine for eval, but a clearly separated non-seeded, auth-enabled install path must exist

**Portability implementations (ADR 0013 Phase 2, still open)**
- [ ] Generic OIDC/JWKS backend token validation behind `get_current_user` (today: `fastapi-azure-auth` only; frontend is already generic per ADR 0028 — backend is the gap)
- [ ] One production-grade non-Azure `SecretStore` (Vault / AWS SM / GCP SM — additive class per ADR 0010)
- [ ] Portable install artifact — Helm chart (ADR 0013's decided shape); the in-repo Terraform is harness-coupled (ADR 0024) and not customer-reusable
- [ ] **G-b** scale-aware execution (#595) — flat-file + UC runners load whole tables into worker pandas; roadmap's own words: "blocks any serious deployment"
- [ ] #725 — rate limiting on the public surface

## Good-to-haves (improve the offer, don't block)

- [ ] README landing polish: screenshots/GIF (currently zero images), customer-voiced pitch above the dev-log status line
- [ ] Prod-ish docker-compose profile (TLS, real auth, non-plaintext secrets) — overlaps the local-first posture work (#591); doubles as the on-prem story
- [ ] Customer-facing upgrade guide (migration-gated deploys exist; the doc doesn't)
- [ ] In-app admin management (G-e: `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` env allowlist is "fine internally, not sellable"); ADR 0026 phase-2 service accounts adjacent
- [ ] Data-access audit trail (G-d/#431) — deploy/README already calls it a prerequisite for regulated (PHI) deployments
- [ ] CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (standard for an OSS project taking contributions)
- [ ] AWS/GCP IaC (#505) → Phase-3 AWS/GCP listings
- [ ] Architecture-review portability nits: #728 (MCP host allowlist), KV purge-protection default

## Sequencing note

The decision + notices + G-i/#729/#730 hygiene items are cheap — do first. The expensive items (generic backend OIDC, non-Azure SecretStore, Helm chart, #595) are exactly ADR 0013 Phase 2 and mostly already scheduled in v1.1 W4–6; the listing slots naturally after them.

You're working in the DataQ repo (FastAPI/Celery backend, structlog logging). Read CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md at the repo root first — they define mandatory working agreements (conventional commits, one-functionality-per-commit, mandatory /code-review before PR, no --no-verify, no force-push, conda env for Python).

## Task: fix GitHub issue #1261

Run `gh issue view 1261` for the full text. Summary: #1226 (PR #1260) fixed a real bug — `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` (`backend/app/alerting/composite.py`) logs a full traceback per failing channel before re-raising the last one; both callers (`backend/app/api/v1/dispatch.py::publish_connection_health` and `backend/app/worker/main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) then logged that SAME traceback a second time. The fix added `mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` helpers (`backend/app/alerting/base.py`) — the composite marks the re-raised exception, and each caller's `except Exception:` block checks the mark to downgrade `log.exception` to `log.warning`.

The concern filed as #1261: that downgrade check (`if was_already_logged(exc): log.warning(...) else: log.exception(...)`) is duplicated verbatim in both callers and is opt-in per caller — a future third caller that forgets the check silently reintroduces the double-traceback bug, with nothing to catch the omission. This repo has an established precedent for this exact class of problem: PII redaction happens ONCE, centrally, in `backend/app/core/logging.py`'s structlog processor chain (see the `_redact_pii` processor there) — not at every call site. #1261 proposes doing the same thing here.

## Suggested direction (from the issue, this is the intended fix — implement it)

Add a structlog processor (alongside `_redact_pii` in `backend/app/core/logging.py`) that:
1. Inspects `event_dict.get("exc_info")` — structlog's convention is this is either `True` (meaning "look up `sys.exc_info()`"), an exception instance, or a `(type, value, tb)` tuple, depending on where in the chain this processor sits and what upstream processors (e.g. `structlog.processors.format_exc_info` or stdlib `ExtraAdder`) have already done to it. Read the current processor chain in `backend/app/core/logging.py` carefully to understand what shape `exc_info` actually has at the point you insert your new processor — get the exception instance out of it correctly (you may need `structlog.processors.ExceptionRenderer`'s internals or `sys.exc_info()` interop, or simpler: structlog's `dict_tracebacks`/`format_exc_info` processors typically run LATE in the chain and expect a real exception; your new processor should run BEFORE those, while `exc_info` is still the raw exception/tuple, not yet rendered to a string).
2. If the extracted exception instance has `was_already_logged(exc)` true (import from `backend.app.alerting.base`), rewrite `event_dict`'s level from `error`/`exception` to `warning`, and drop `exc_info` from the dict (so it doesn't also render a traceback).
3. Otherwise pass `event_dict` through unchanged.
4. Then simplify `dispatch.py::publish_connection_health` and `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop` back to unconditional `log.exception(...)` — remove their per-caller `was_already_logged` checks, since the processor now does the downgrade for any caller automatically.

Be careful about import direction: `backend/app/core/logging.py` is a low-level core module; `backend/app/alerting/base.py` is a higher-level domain module. Check whether `core/logging.py` importing from `app/alerting/` creates a circular import or violates a layering convention in this codebase (grep for existing `core/logging.py` imports and what imports `core/logging.py` early in app startup) — if it's a problem, consider whether `mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` should move to a lower-level shared module instead (but only do this if actually necessary; check first, don't over-engineer).

## Acceptance criteria (from the issue — must hold)

- A third (or later) caller of the composite's delivered-first methods gets the downgrade automatically, with no per-caller opt-in required.
- The two existing call sites (`dispatch.py`, `main.py`) simplify back to unconditional `log.exception(...)`.
- The existing #1226 regression tests (which assert `log_level`/`exc_info` via structlog's `capture_logs` test helper — grep for them, likely in `backend/tests/alerting/` or `backend/tests/api/`/`backend/tests/worker/`) still pass UNCHANGED, proving the observable behavior is identical — just relocated.
- Add a new test proving the processor-chain approach: a THIRD, synthetic caller (not `dispatch.py`/`main.py`) that raises an already-marked exception through `log.exception(...)` gets the same downgrade with no opt-in code at that call site — this is the actual regression test for what #1261 fixes (the previous architecture couldn't have passed this test without editing the third caller).

## Process (follow CLAUDE.md §6 working agreements)

1. Create a branch `fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade` off `main`.
2. Read `backend/app/core/logging.py` (full file — processor chain, `_redact_pii`, and however exc_info/tracebacks are currently rendered), `backend/app/alerting/base.py` (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged`), `backend/app/alerting/composite.py` (`_fan_out_delivered_first`), `backend/app/api/v1/dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `backend/app/worker/main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`, and the existing #1226 regression tests, before changing anything.
3. Implement the processor, simplify both callers, add the new third-caller test.
4. Verify locally BEFORE committing: Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit, and the relevant pytest modules (alerting, dispatch, worker main, and core/logging tests).
5. Commit with a conventional commit message (`refactor: ...`), referencing #1261.
6. Push and open a PR via `gh pr create` with `Fixes #1261` in the body. Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` if present.
7. Spawn the `/code-review` skill/slash-command on your own diff (mandatory — never only inline self-review); if unavailable use the `pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer` agent type. Fix in-scope findings; file a GitHub issue via `gh issue create` for anything you consciously decide to defer (never drop a finding silently — CLAUDE.md §11 "every finding ends fixed or filed").
8. Do NOT merge — leave the PR open for CI + human merge.

## Report back

PR URL, one-line summary, confirmation local verification passed, what code-review found (if anything), and any circular-import issue you hit and how you resolved it.
