input.prompt:
You're working in the DataQ repo (FastAPI/Celery backend, pytest test suite). Read CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md at the repo root first — mandatory working agreements (conventional commits, one-functionality-per-commit, mandatory /code-review before PR, no force-push, conda env, test coverage discipline).

## Task: fix GitHub issue #1270

Run `gh issue view 1270` for the full text. Summary: #1251 introduced a shared `FakeSecretStore` + `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper in `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py`, meant to replace every hand-rolled `SecretStore` test double scattered across the test suite. #1251 only migrated 5 files. Issue #1270 lists ~31 remaining files (both an original list and an expanded follow-up list — the full set is in the issue body) that still hand-roll their own fake `SecretStore`.

## Your job

1. Read `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py` in full first — understand `FakeSecretStore`'s constructor shape (currently `raise_on_write: bool` per the issue) and `override_secret_store(app, store)`'s exact contract (why a bare dependency-override assignment is buggy — read the module's docstring, it explains a real bug this helper avoids).
2. Read the full file list in the issue body (`gh issue view 1270`) — both the "Originally named" and "Found in the follow-up review pass" sections, ~31 files total under `backend/tests/`.
3. For EACH file: find its local hand-rolled `SecretStore` double (grep for class definitions implementing the `SecretStore` interface, or local fixture functions returning ad-hoc store objects), migrate it to import and use `FakeSecretStore` + `override_secret_store`, and delete the local class/fixture.
4. Two files need special handling, called out explicitly in the issue — read these carefully, don't just blind-swap:
   - `backend/tests/core/test_seed_local_smtp_secret.py::_FakeStore` is MORE GENERAL than today's `FakeSecretStore` (it supports `raise_on_get: Exception | None` / `raise_on_set: Exception | None` independently, vs. today's single `raise_on_write: bool`). The issue suggests generalizing `FakeSecretStore`'s constructor to match this richer, already-proven shape (`raise_on_get`/`raise_on_set` as optional exceptions) rather than force-fitting this file down to the narrower shape. Do this generalization in `fake_secret_store.py` itself (keep it backward compatible for existing callers using `raise_on_write` if that's cheap, or migrate all call sites to the new shape if that's cleaner — your call, but keep every existing test passing).
   - `backend/tests/services/test_notification_service.py` has a `_SoftDeleteStore(_FakeStore)` subclass (~line 255) implementing a distinct behavior (soft-delete semantics). Mirror this as a small subclass of `FakeSecretStore` in the same pattern established for other distinct-behavior cases (e.g. however `_WriteFailStore` or similar already exists, if it does — check `fake_secret_store.py` for existing subclass precedent) rather than reinventing a one-off.
5. This is a large, mechanical, low-risk sweep — the goal is 100% migration of every file listed in the issue, not a partial pass. Work through the list methodically; use TodoWrite-style tracking internally (a simple checklist in your own working notes) so you don't lose track across ~31 files. If, after starting, you find the true scope is meaningfully larger than the issue describes (e.g. many more undiscovered hand-rolled doubles), that's fine — sweep those too; the goal (per the issue's own framing) is "delete every hand-rolled `SecretStore` double", not just satisfy the exact list.
6. After migrating, grep the whole `backend/tests/` tree for any remaining hand-rolled `SecretStore`-implementing class that ISN'T `FakeSecretStore` (or one of its now-established subclasses) to confirm the sweep is actually complete before declaring done.

## Process (follow CLAUDE.md §6 working agreements)

1. Create a branch `chore/issue-1270-consolidate-secret-store-doubles` off `main`.
2. Do the sweep as described.
3. Verify locally BEFORE committing: Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit, and run the FULL backend test suite (`pytest backend/tests/`) — not just a subset, since this touches ~31 test files and a shared fixture; a full run is the only way to be confident nothing broke. This may take a while; that's expected and correct for this change's blast radius.
4. Commit with a conventional commit message (`chore: ...` or `test: ...`), referencing #1270. This is one coherent functionality (test-double consolidation) even though it's one big commit across many files — that matches CLAUDE.md's "one functionality per commit" rule, not a violation of it.
5. Push and open a PR via `gh pr create` with `Fixes #1270` in the body. Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` if present. In the PR body, list which files were migrated and note the `FakeSecretStore` constructor generalization if you made one.
6. Spawn the `/code-review` skill/slash-command on your own diff (mandatory — never only inline self-review); if unavailable use `pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer`. Given the size of this diff, expect the review to take a while and possibly find a few real issues (e.g. a migrated test that now behaves subtly differently because the old hand-rolled double had an undocumented quirk `FakeSecretStore` doesn't replicate) — fix genuine in-scope findings; file a GitHub issue for anything you consciously decide to defer.
7. Do NOT merge — leave the PR open for CI + human merge.

## Report back

PR URL, the full list of files migrated (confirm it covers the issue's list), confirmation the FULL backend test suite passes locally, whether you generalized `FakeSecretStore`'s constructor and how, and what code-review found (if anything).

@@ -146,6 +146,86 @@ def _add_request_id(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDic
     return event_dict
 
 
+def _extract_exc_info_exception(raw: Any) -> BaseException | None:
+    """Pull the exception instance out of an ``exc_info`` value, whatever shape it
+    currently has. structlog callers set ``exc_info`` to ``True`` (``BoundLogger.
+    exception()``'s default), a bare exception instance, or a ``(type, value, tb)``
+    tuple (what ``ProcessorFormatter`` copies over from a foreign stdlib
+    ``LogRecord.exc_info``) — the shape depends on where in the chain a processor
+    sits and who produced the record. Mirrors structlog's own internal
+    ``processors._figure_out_exc_info`` (used by ``format_exc_info``/
+    ``dict_tracebacks``) rather than importing that private helper directly."""
+    if isinstance(raw, BaseException):
+        return raw
+    if isinstance(raw, tuple) and len(raw) == 3 and isinstance(raw[1], BaseException):
+        return raw[1]
+    if raw:
+        # `True` (or any other truthy sentinel): "look up the exception currently
+        # being handled", the stdlib `exc_info=True` convention.
+        return sys.exc_info()[1]
+    return None
+
+
+def _downgrade_already_logged_exceptions(
+    _logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict
+) -> EventDict:
+    """Downgrade a log record whose exception was already reported with a full
+    traceback elsewhere, so a caller never has to remember to check that itself.
+
+    #1226 fixed a real bug: when every alerting channel fails,
+    ``CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first`` (``alerting/composite.py``)
+    logs a full traceback per failing channel before re-raising the last one, and
+    the caller's own ``except Exception: log.exception(...)`` logged that SAME
+    traceback a second time. The fix (#1260) added
+    ``alerting.base.mark_already_logged``/``was_already_logged`` and had each
+    caller check it before choosing ``log.warning`` over ``log.exception``. #1261:
+    that check was duplicated verbatim in both callers and opt-in per caller — a
+    future third caller that forgets it silently reintroduces the exact bug, with
+    nothing to catch the omission.
+
+    This is the same shape as PII redaction (CLAUDE.md §10 / #849): the fix
+    belongs in the processor chain, applied to EVERY log record once, not
+    repeated at every call site. Any caller's ``log.exception(...)`` — including
+    a foreign (non-structlog) ``logging.exception(...)`` bridged in via
+    ``foreign_pre_chain`` — gets the downgrade for free.
+
+    Must run AFTER ``add_log_level`` (so there is a ``level`` to overwrite) and
+    BEFORE the exception is rendered to a string (``_dict_tracebacks_no_locals``)
+    — while ``event_dict["exc_info"]`` is still the raw shape, not yet consumed.
+
+    Dropping ``exc_info`` also drops the traceback, which was the only place the
+    exception's TYPE was visible on the downgraded line (`_poll_staleness_loop`'s
+    original comment on this, #1260 review) — restored here as ``error_type`` so
+    every downgraded caller keeps that correlator, not just the ones that used to
+    remember to add it by hand. ``setdefault`` so a caller-supplied ``error_type``
+    (a different meaning in a future call site) is never clobbered.
+    """
+    exc = _extract_exc_info_exception(event_dict.get("exc_info"))
+    if exc is None:
+        return event_dict
+
+    # Lazy import: `core/logging.py` is a foundational module imported very early
+    # (module scope of `main.py`, `worker/main.py`, every datasource/alerting
+    # module for `get_logger`); `alerting/base.py` is a higher-level domain
+    # module. It has no import-time dependency back on `core.logging` itself (its
+    # only DataQ import is `db.models`, and the `alerting` package's `__init__.py`
+    # is docstring-only), so this does not actually cycle — but keeping the
+    # import inside the guarded, exception-only branch means the rest of the app
+    # never pays for or depends on the domain import at module-load time, and a
+    # future edit to `alerting/base.py` that adds its own `core.logging` import
+    # (every one of its sibling files in that package already does, for
+    # `get_logger`) can't turn this into a real cycle.
+    from backend.app.alerting.base import was_already_logged
+
+    if not was_already_logged(exc):
+        return event_dict
+

+    event_dict.pop("exc_info", None)
+    return event_dict
+

@@ -281,6 +361,9 @@ def configure_logging(service_name: str = "dataq") -> None:
         structlog.processors.add_log_level,

+        # before `_dict_tracebacks_no_locals` below (exc_info must still be raw).
+        _downgrade_already_logged_exceptions,

refactor: centralize the already-logged-traceback downgrade in the structlog processor chain

CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first logs a full traceback per failing
alert channel before re-raising the last one (#1226/#1260), and each caller
re-checked was_already_logged() by hand to avoid double-logging it. That check
was duplicated verbatim across dispatch.py and worker/main.py and was opt-in
per caller, so a future third caller could silently reintroduce the bug.

Move the downgrade into a new _downgrade_already_logged_exceptions structlog
processor, mirroring how PII redaction is centralized in the same chain
(CLAUDE.md §10 / #849) instead of repeated at call sites. Both existing
callers simplify back to unconditional log.exception(...).

Fixes #1261
EOF

## Summary

- `core_table`'s 3-part (`catalog.schema.table`) form used to embed `catalog`
  and `schema` as one *unquoted* string, so the #476 mixed-case quoting fix
  only ever reached the table — a mixed-case Unity Catalog catalog/schema
  silently folded. Fixed by making `core_table` dialect-aware for this path:
  every part (catalog, schema, table) goes through the same case-based
  quoting decision as `folding_identifier`, and a part that needs quoting is
  wrapped with the dialect's own `identifier_preparer.quote_identifier` —
  never a hardcoded `"` or backtick.
- Along the way, found that Snowflake's own SQLAlchemy dialect *already*
  special-cases a dotted schema string (`quote_schema` re-splits it and
  re-derives quoting from one whole-string flag, discarding embedded quote
  characters) — so the straightforward "assemble a pre-quoted string, put it
  in `schema=`" approach silently undid the fix on the one dialect it's for.
  The fix instead folds the whole pre-quoted namespace into Core's
  **table-name** slot with `schema=None`, which has no such override.

    if spec.query is not None:
        q = _wrapped_query(spec)
        # Interpolation is safe: `q` passed the read-only single-statement
        # validator (ADR 0019) at author time AND immediately above. The
        # newline before the closing paren keeps a trailing `-- comment` (legal
        # per the validator) from swallowing the wrapper's tail.
        # Both suppressions below are load-bearing (Ruff S608 and bandit B608 each
        # flag the f-string). They are bare by convention (#806): bandit parses
        # trailing prose as test ids, and Ruff rejects a malformed directive the same
        # way — so neither marker is ever spelled inside an explanatory comment.
        count_sql = f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (\n{q}\n) __dataq_src"  # noqa: S608  # nosec B608
        select_sql = (
            f"SELECT * FROM (\n{q}\n) __dataq_src "  # noqa: S608  # nosec B608
            f"LIMIT {int(max_rows) + 1}"
        )
        count_stmt = sa.text(count_sql)
        select_stmt = sa.text(select_sql)
    else:
        if not spec.table:
            raise DatasetReadUnsupportedError(
                "SQL comparison side needs a table (or a query)", detail={"spec": "table"}
            )
        if connection.type == "unity_catalog" and not spec.catalog:
            # The UC engine URL deliberately pins no catalog (profiler parity) —
            # an unqualified 2-part name would resolve against the session
            # default catalog and silently read the wrong table.
            raise DatasetReadUnsupportedError(

        schema = resolve_effective_schema(connection, spec.schema)

        count_stmt = sa.select(sa.func.count()).select_from(source)
        select_stmt = sa.select(sa.text("*")).select_from(source).limit(max_rows + 1)

## Report

**Angle 1 — Altitude**

1. **`backend/app/datasources/sql.py:150-159` (`core_table`, lines ~226-231)** — The whole mechanism depends on two undocumented internal behaviors: `IdentifierPreparer.quote()` special-casing a `quoted_name(..., quote=False)` marker to skip its own reserved-word/quote-necessity logic, and `format_table()`'s `effective_schema = schema_for_object(table)` being falsy only because `schema=None` is passed. Neither is part of SQLAlchemy's documented composition contract for "pre-assemble a multi-part namespace." *Failure scenario:* a future SQLAlchemy point release that changes how `format_table` treats a table whose "name" already contains dots (e.g. adding its own dot-splitting for compatibility with 3-part BigQuery names) would silently re-break exactly the case this PR fixes, and nothing would catch it except the dialect-specific unit tests already in the repo — there's no invariant test asserting the underlying `quoted_name`/`schema=None` contract itself.

2. **`sql.py` — routing around `SnowflakeIdentifierPreparer.quote_schema`** — confirmed live (read the installed `snowflake-sqlalchemy` source): `quote_schema` re-splits any dotted schema string via `_split_schema_by_dot` and re-derives quoting from scratch, discarding embedded quote characters. The fix works around this by never using the `schema=` slot at all, rather than fixing/overriding the one behavior that's actually broken. *Maintenance cost:* every future dialect this project onboards for a catalog-bearing datasource (ADR 0038 roadmap mentions BigQuery/Dataplex) must be manually verified not to have its own dotted-schema re-splitting, since there's no mechanism enforcing that "route through the table slot" stays valid — the docstring says "every dialect tested" (Snowflake, Databricks, SQLAlchemy default), which is a testing claim, not a guarantee.

3. **`_quote_namespace_part` (`sql.py` ~line 130-144) duplicates `folding_identifier`'s case check** (`name == name.lower()`) instead of calling it. Two independent implementations of the same "should I quote" decision. *Failure scenario:* if `folding_identifier`'s case rule is ever changed (e.g., locale-aware casefold, or handling of digits-only names), `_quote_namespace_part` silently drifts out of sync since nothing ties them together beyond a docstring comment.

4. **`dialect: Dialect | None = None` threaded through 4 files** (`sql.py`, `monitors.py`, `anomaly.py`, `profile_service.py`), each independently re-deriving `dialect = conn.dialect if catalog is not None else None` at the call site (`anomaly.py:~135`, `profile_service.py:~489,~1039`). This is runtime-conditional, not type-enforced — a future caller that passes `catalog` without `dialect` only discovers the bug via a `ValueError` when a catalog-qualified check actually runs, not at type-check time. *Concrete cost:* a 5th catalog-taking call site added later has no static signal reminding it to thread `dialect`; it will type-check fine and fail only at runtime on a UC-qualified target.

5. Per the project's own standing lesson recorded in `MEMORY.md` ("for anything whose type or value crosses a driver boundary, only a live run is evidence" — directly born from #953/#937, the *same* quoting subsystem), this PR's verification is unit-test SQL-string rendering against in-process dialect objects only (Snowflake, Databricks, default) — no live run against a real mixed-case Unity Catalog table is mentioned in the diff or PR. This is exactly the failure class (`quote_schema` behavior, driver-specific `IdentifierPreparer` quirks) that has bitten this codebase before while unit tests stayed green.

<result>## Findings

**One solid, well-evidenced bug — the "downgrade" is cosmetic for anything that reads the real `logging.LogRecord`, not the structlog event_dict.**

- **File:** `backend/app/core/logging.py`, `_downgrade_already_logged_exceptions` (lines 169–226), wired into `shared_processors` (line 366), consumed by `_configure_otel_log_export`'s `_RedactingOTelLogHandler._get_attributes` (lines 288–290) and `LoggingHandler._translate` (opentelemetry-sdk).
- **Root cause:** Both callers now always invoke `log.exception(...)`/`logger.exception(...)`. Traced through `structlog`'s stdlib `BoundLogger._proxy_to_logger` → `getattr(self._logger, "exception")(*args, **kw)` → stdlib `logging.Logger.exception()`, which unconditionally sets `exc_info=True` and logs at `self.error(...)`. This fixes `record.levelno=40 (ERROR)` and populates `record.exc_info` with the real traceback **at record-creation time, before any structlog processor runs**, and this is completely independent of what a processor later writes into the `event_dict`. Verified empirically (`python3` repro): `logging.Logger.exception()` always yields `levelno=40, exc_info set=True`, regardless of message content. The old per-caller code called the genuinely different `log.warning(...)` method for the downgraded case, which produced a real WARNING-level record with no `exc_info` at all — that guarantee is lost in the refactor.
- **Manifestation A — severity split-brain:** `opentelemetry.sdk._logs.LoggingHandler._translate` computes `severity_number = std_to_otel(record.levelno)` / `severity_text = record.levelname` straight off the LogRecord, not the JSON body. Every "downgraded" record (stdout JSON shows `"level": "warning"`) is still exported to App Insights/OTel as ERROR severity.
  - *Failure scenario:* every alert channel fails → `publish_connection_health` (dispatch.py:106) or `_poll_staleness_loop` (main.py:88) logs `.exception(...)` on the marked exception → stdout correctly shows `warning`, but App Insights receives an ERROR/Exception-severity record — the exact duplicate-alert noise #1226 was meant to eliminate is unchanged on that channel.
- **Manifestation B — traceback re-leaks via OTel attributes:** `LoggingHandler._get_attributes` (base class, called by the app's `_RedactingOTelLogHandler`) reads `record.exc_info` directly (not `event_dict["exc_info"]`, which the processor already popped) and unconditionally sets `exception.type`, `exception.message`, and a full `exception.stacktrace` (`traceback.format_exception(*record.exc_info)`) attribute. `_redact_pii` scrubs known secret/PII patterns but does not suppress a full traceback.
  - *Failure scenario:* same as above — the composite already logged this traceback once per channel (#1226's original problem); the "downgraded" call still ships the full type/message/stacktrace to OTel/App Insights as log attributes, so the duplicate-traceback problem is reintroduced on the telemetry channel even though stdout looks fixed.

The new tests (`test_downgrades_a_marked_exception_from_any_caller` etc.) only assert against `capsys`-captured stdout JSON, so they cannot and do not catch either manifestation — no OTel exporter/handler is exercised in the test suite.

No other candidates from the ordering, malformed-`exc_info`-shape, or cross-call-site-marker-leak angles rose above speculative — the ordering is correct in both the native and foreign chains, and the two current callers both swallow (never re-raise) the marked exception, so no live re-logging-elsewhere path exists today.</result>

            # `opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging` — which only injects trace
            # context into records; it is NOT an export bridge. The sdk handler IS
            # the bridge (it's what the azure-monitor distro uses under the hood).
            # Suppress just that message so an unrelated deprecation still surfaces.
            warnings.filterwarnings(
                "ignore", message=r".*LoggingHandler.*", category=DeprecationWarning
            )
            handler = _RedactingOTelLogHandler(level=level, logger_provider=provider)
        # Same redacting ProcessorFormatter as stdout, so records exported to the
        # backend pass through `_redact_pii` (incl. the secret-string scrubber) — a
        # foreign record carrying a secret in its message is scrubbed before export
        # (#494). App-level structlog records are already redacted upstream.
        handler.setFormatter(formatter)
        # Break the exporter's feedback loop AT THE BRIDGE (#852).
        #
        # `azure.core`'s HTTP policy logs a request AND a response line for every call the
        # SDK makes — including the exporter's own uploads. Those records reach root,
        # re-enter this handler, are exported, and generate more uploads. Measured in prod
        # at ~10/sec.
        #
        # Setting that logger's level was not enough: it works in the API but NOT in the
        # Celery worker, where something in the worker/prefork logging setup restores INFO.
        # Rather than keep chasing who resets it, drop the records here, at the one place
        # they must pass through to reach the backend. A filter on the handler cannot be
        # defeated by a level reset elsewhere.
        #
        # Only the EXPORT is filtered — the records still reach stdout, so a real transport
        # problem is still visible in the container log.
        handler.addFilter(lambda record: not record.name.startswith("azure.core"))
        root.addHandler(handler)

        # Break the feedback loop: the SDK/exporter log their own "failed to export"
        # warnings on these namespaces; propagated to root they re-enter THIS bridge
        # and get re-queued for export — an amplifier that fires exactly when the
        # backend is unreachable. Keep them off the export pipeline (a well-known
        # OTel root-bridge footgun).
        for noisy in ("opentelemetry", "azure.monitor.opentelemetry"):
            logging.getLogger(noisy).propagate = False

        # Positive confirmation so "my logs never reached the backend" is diagnosable
        # (misconfig looks identical to telemetry-off otherwise). Endpoint is infra
        # config, not a secret; the App Insights connection string is NOT logged.
        logging.getLogger(__name__).info(
            "otel_log_export_configured service=%s exporters=%d azure=%s otlp=%s",
            service_name,
            len(exporters),
            bool(settings.applicationinsights_connection_string),
            settings.otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint or "off",
        )
    except Exception:
        # Degrade to stdout-only rather than take the process down (the #405 blast
        # radius: orchestration polling / scheduled dispatch / gap recovery / purge).
        logging.getLogger(__name__).exception("otel_log_export_setup_failed")


def configure_logging(service_name: str = "dataq") -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)

    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [
        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
        _add_request_id,
        structlog.processors.add_log_level,
        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
        _redact_pii,
        # Must run after `add_log_level` (there's a `level` to overwrite) and
        # before `_dict_tracebacks_no_locals` below (exc_info must still be raw).
        _downgrade_already_logged_exceptions,
    ]

    # Bridge stdlib logging (uvicorn.access, uvicorn.error, etc.) through the
    # same processor chain so every line out of the app is JSON with a
    # request_id when available. Without this the uvicorn access log emits
    # human-readable text that App Insights can't correlate (#50).
    formatter = structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter(
        foreign_pre_chain=shared_processors,
        processors=[
            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.remove_processors_meta,
            _dict_tracebacks_no_locals,
            # Re-run the redactor AFTER the traceback is rendered to a dict —
            # the pre-chain pass ran before the exception existed as strings, so
            # exception messages/frames never met the scrubber (#536). Idempotent
            # on everything else.
            _redact_pii,
            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),
        ],
    )

    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    handler.setFormatter(formatter)
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers = [handler]
    root.setLevel(level)

    # `azure.core`'s HTTP logging policy logs a full request AND response line for EVERY
    # HTTP call the Azure SDK makes — Key Vault reads, and (once the OTel bridge below is
    # attached) the exporter's own uploads to App Insights. That last one is a
    # self-sustaining amplifier: the upload is logged, the log record reaches root,
    # re-enters the export bridge, is uploaded, and is logged again. Measured in prod at
    # ~10 records/second — 19,000 in half an hour — which drowned the application's real
    # logs (a genuine orchestration-poll event became unfindable in the noise) and burned
    # ingestion quota (#852).
    #
    # Silenced at INFO rather than detached (`propagate = False`), so a genuine transport
    # WARNING from the SDK still reaches stdout and the backend; only the per-request
    # chatter that feeds the loop is dropped.
    logging.getLogger("azure.core.pipeline.policies.http_logging_policy").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

    # Detach uvicorn's pre-configured handlers; let logs propagate to root so
    # they hit the structlog ProcessorFormatter above.
    for name in ("uvicorn", "uvicorn.error"):
        uvicorn_logger = logging.getLogger(name)
        uvicorn_logger.handlers = []
        uvicorn_logger.propagate = True

# CLAUDE.md — DataQ project guide for AI assistants

> Single source of truth for any Claude / AI assistant working in this repo. Read this end-to-end before touching code.

---

## 1. Project summary

**DataQ** is a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **5 datasources** and integrates with **3 orchestration providers**.

| Layer | Components |
|---|---|
| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3 **and any S3-compatible store** (MinIO/Ceph/R2/Wasabi/Backblaze, via the optional `endpoint_url` — #1063), Unity Catalog (Databricks), Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030) |
| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow, dbt (ADR 0029) |
| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor (generic OIDC — `oidc-client-ts`) |
| **Auth / secrets** | Three-mode ladder (ADR 0032): dev-bypass (eval) · **email OTP** (IdP-less, default for the local stack — #1150) · OIDC (Azure AD validated; provider-neutral `AUTH_*` contract) — plus PATs (`dq_live_`) for API/MCP clients. Secrets: Azure Key Vault / OpenBao (ADR 0039) |
| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps (API + worker + frontend; frontend is the sole public surface, api internal — ADR 0028 §5) |
| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
| **AI integration** | FastMCP (8 curated tools mounted at `/mcp`) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |

Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.

---

## 2. Architecture at a glance

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the full diagram (Mermaid — renders on GitHub).

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► Frontend Container App (nginx SPA, sole public ingress)
AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► │  proxies /api + /mcp + /healthz same-origin
                         ▼
                    FastAPI (Container Apps, INTERNAL ingress) ──► PostgreSQL
                         │  │
                         │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
                         ├──► Redis (task queue)
                         ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
                         └──► App Insights (observability)

ADF ──► Azure Monitor alert rule ──► webhook ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf ──► (proxied) api
Airflow ──► on_success/on_failure_callback ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow ──► (proxied) api
FastAPI ──► MS Teams / Slack / email (alerts, ResultPublisher seam)
```

---

## 3. Repo layout

Flat monorepo (decided in Week 1):

```
DataQ/
├── backend/                     # FastAPI + Celery + GX (Python, conda)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── core/                # logging, errors, config (locked in PR 2)
│   │   ├── db/                  # SQLAlchemy models, session
│   │   ├── api/                 # FastAPI routers (versioned: /api/v1/...)
│   │   ├── services/            # business logic per domain
│   │   ├── orchestration/       # OrchestrationProvider abstraction (ADF, Airflow)
│   │   ├── datasources/         # ConnectionAdapter + CheckRunner per type; gx_runner.py (shared GX translation), flatfile.py (flat-file IO + runner + batch resolution), sql.py (shared SQL-identifier allowlist — #428)
│   │   └── mcp/                 # FastMCP tools (Week 7)
│   ├── alembic/
│   └── tests/                   # + tests/support/ (adversarial harness), tests/integration/ (end-to-end datasource runs)
├── frontend/                    # React + Vite + Ant Design (Node, pnpm)
│   ├── src/
│   └── tests/
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md          # Mermaid architecture diagram
│   └── adr/                     # Architecture Decision Records
├── integrations/                # user-deployed snippets (NOT app code; e.g. Airflow DAG callback)
│   └── airflow/                 # dataq_airflow_callback.py + setup README
├── scripts/
│   └── setup.sh                 # one-command dev env bootstrap
├── context/                     # original product/roadmap context (read-only reference)
│   └── DataQ_platform_roadmap.md
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/
│   ├── pull_request_template.md
│   ├── CODEOWNERS
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
├── docker-compose.yml
├── environment.yml              # conda env — pip section points at backend/requirements-dev.txt
├── pyproject.toml               # Black + Ruff + mypy config
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── CLAUDE.md                    # this file
└── README.md
```

**Promotion to `apps/` + `packages/`:** only if a real shared package emerges (e.g., auto-generated OpenAPI client in Week 4–5). Default flat.

---

## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction

**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
- AWS S3 — and any S3-compatible store, via the connection's optional `endpoint_url` (#1063)
- Unity Catalog / Databricks
- Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030; engine-registered Iceberg tables also work zero-code under the `snowflake`/`unity_catalog` connections)

**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:

1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.

All three providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second, dbt (ADR 0029) is the third (artifact-poll + HMAC callback, no host REST API). **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**

| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
| dbt | post-build callback → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (app-level signing key) | poll `run_results.json` artifact (adls/s3/file), 10 min |

Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.

**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.

---

## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1

- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor. Every v1 check is a GX **expectation** (`check.kind = 'expectation'`).
- **v1.1+:** platform-native engines are **connection-anchored** (ADR [0036](docs/adr/0036-connection-anchored-check-engines.md)): every datasource connection offers GX; a Snowflake connection additionally offers **DMF**, Unity Catalog offers **DQX** (DLT/streaming — GX is batch-only), a future BigQuery type offers **Dataplex**. Engine selection is **per check** (`check.engine`, default `gx`, validated against the connection's capability set; `kind` stays orthogonal to `engine`) — supersedes the earlier suite-level `engine: gx | dqx` toggle sketch. DMF is the first native build; DQX/Dataplex are trigger-gated (see the ADR §6).
- **Monitor-kind seam (do-now, Week 3):** not every monitor is a GX expectation. A `check.kind` discriminator (`expectation` in v1; `freshness | volume | schema_drift | anomaly | comparison` reserved — freshness/volume shipped post-v1 (#426/#437) and **`comparison` shipped v1.1 W3** (ADR 0015, #791–#795) and **`schema_drift` shipped v1.1 W4** (#592) and **`anomaly` shipped v1.1 W5** (#593, rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality, PRs #1117/#1119)) + numeric `metric_value` on results let v1.x auto-monitors slot in without a check/result schema rewrite. This seam is **orthogonal to the datasource seams** (`CheckRunner`, `ConnectionAdapter`): it varies by *monitor kind*, not datasource. See ADR `0012` (and `0014` for the reserved `comparison` / cross-dataset reconciliation kind) and post-v1 roadmap Theme A. Most real incidents are freshness/volume, not value-level — this is the leap from "GX runner" to DQ platform.
- **DQ-dimension axis (v1.1 W4, ADR [0038](docs/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md)):** every check also carries a `dimension` — accuracy / completeness / consistency / integrity / timeliness / uniqueness / validity — a **third axis orthogonal to both `kind` (how the monitor works) and `engine` (what evaluates it)**. Closed vocabulary via table `CHECK`; derived by default from the check type, **stored** (so #889 aggregates in SQL and an override survives), and overridable at any time. Derivation is **deliberately partial** — `accuracy`/`integrity` are never derivable from a rule shape and custom SQL is an arbitrary predicate — so **NULL means unclassified and must render as a coverage gap**, never silently bucketed. Existing rows were backfilled (#952, §5 amended). It is the input to the asset DQ scorecard (#889), whose value is *coverage* ("this asset has no Timeliness checks") more than score.
- **Week-3 outcome (done):** the UC run path is thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` (reads the table into a GX DataFrame asset — the DQX swap-in shape), and `check.kind` + `metric_value`/`duration_ms` shipped in the one threshold migration, so the monitor-kind impls won't ripple into the suite/check/result layer later. **Amended v1.1 W6 (#1179):** the UC runner now builds **two** batches — the DataFrame one for every ordinary expectation, and a GX **Databricks-SQL** batch for custom-SQL checks only. `UnexpectedRowsExpectation`'s metrics have a SqlAlchemy provider and no pandas one, so ADR 0019's UC support had never once worked in a run *or* a dry-run; it is SQL by definition and was never going to be a DQX rule, so the DQX swap-in argument is unaffected for everything it actually covers.

---

## 6. Working agreements (rules above feature work)

Full list (40 rules across 8 categories) lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Highlights:

### Commit & change discipline
Per-functionality workflow, in order:
1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible).
2. **Test coverage for the functionality** (unit/integration as applicable — the ≥80% CI gate, live since Week 8, covers this).
3. **Docs updated if required** (CLAUDE.md / ADR / CONTRIBUTING / user docs — whichever the change touches).
4. **Agentic code-review on the PR** — spawn `/code-review` (never an inline self-review only) and post findings to the PR as inline comments (`/code-review --comment`).
5. **Fix issues found in the same PR** where feasible.
6. **File a GitHub issue for anything deferred** — never drop a finding silently. Use `gh issue create`; the fixing PR must include `Fixes #N`.
7. **Full CI gate must pass** (lint/format/types/tests/security — see below).
8. **Squash-merge to `main`.**

### Git workflow
- **Trunk-based** with short-lived feature branches off `main`. No long-lived `develop`.
- Branch names: `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, `docs/<desc>`.
- `main` is protected: PR + passing CI + no force-push. (≥1 approving review is disabled during solo-dev phase; re-enable before onboarding a second contributor.)
- **Squash-merge only into `main`.**
- **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`).

### CI/CD quality gates (block merge)
- Ruff (lint), Black `--check` (format), mypy (types), pytest (from W8), frontend lint/format/test.
- `betterleaks` secret scanning (pre-commit + CI).
- Bandit (Python SAST) + CodeQL.
- **Dependency CVE audit (CI): `pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (full backend runtime + test surface) + `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` (frontend).** Synchronous merge gate; complements the async Dependabot layer below.
- **Python deps have one source of truth: `backend/requirements.txt`** (runtime hub) → `requirements-dev.txt` (`-r` it + test toolchain) → `environment.yml` + CI all install from it. The re-listed subsets `requirements-dev.txt` pulls are `requirements-typecheck.txt` (the typed deps mypy needs) and `requirements-tooling.txt` (Black/Ruff/mypy/Bandit/pre-commit); the `typecheck-deps-sync` check (pre-commit **and** CI `backend-lint`) keeps the mypy hook aligned. `requirements-mutation.txt` (mutmut) is **standalone — not `-r`'d by anything**, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` surface (manual tool, CONTRIBUTING rule 4a). Bump a Python version in `requirements.txt` only.
- Dependabot for npm + pip + github-actions — **version updates + security alerts/updates both enabled** (alerts scan the full pip+npm dependency graph).

### Tooling (locked in Week 1, do not drift)
- **Python:** conda env (`conda create -n dataq python=3.13`) — *not* venv, *not* poetry. (3.13 since ADR 0017; was 3.11.)
- **Black** formatter (CI-enforced).
- **Ruff** lint, **mypy** types, **structlog** logging, **Pydantic Settings** config (12-factor).
- **Frontend:** Prettier + ESLint.

### Observability
- **Structured logging from Week 1.** structlog, JSON, `request_id` correlation propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX.
- **PII redaction at logger level** (failed-check sample rows may contain sensitive data).
- **App Insights exception tracking wired Week 1**, not Week 7.

### Database
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward.
- Migration PR checklist: rollback plan + "tested up + down locally."

### Documentation
- **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** — one short markdown per significant decision.
- `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from clone to working dev env.

### Security cadence
- End-of-week quick scan from Week 2: vuln alerts (Dependabot alerts + CI `pip-audit`/`pnpm audit`), secret scan, OWASP spot check, Key Vault audit.
- Hard security review gate before Week 7 deploy.

---

## 7. Required reading before coding

1. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — full 40-rule working agreements + DoD + commit/branch conventions
2. [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) — all ADRs (architecture decisions with rationale)
3. [context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md](context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md) — the 8-week, 100-task product roadmap
4. The current week's milestone target (see §13 below)

---

## 8. Local dev quickstart

> **Note:** `scripts/setup.sh` prompts for your sign-in email on first run (the local stack defaults to **email OTP** with a bundled Mailpit inbox at `http://localhost:8025` — #1150; answer blank for the explicit dev-bypass downgrade) and generates local credentials into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app`.

```bash
git clone <repo>
cd DataQ
./scripts/setup.sh           # creates conda env, installs pre-commit, pulls images, runs migrations, seeds dev data
conda activate dataq
docker-compose up            # Postgres + Redis + FastAPI + React + Celery worker
# Smoke test:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/_probe/snowflake-suite
# …then read the run through the REAL API (the probe's own reader was removed in
# #1039 — it had no suite-ownership check):
curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/runs/<run_id>
# Browse Swagger: http://localhost:8000/docs
```

---

## 9. Key design decisions (ADR index)

The full decision index — one line per ADR with status, 0001–0040 to date — lives at **[docs/adr/README.md](docs/adr/README.md)** and is the **single source of truth** (this section used to duplicate it as a table and the two drifted; it no longer does). Read the index before coding and open the individual ADR whenever a decision bears on your change. The day-to-day operating rules those decisions distill into are already captured in §4–§6, §10 and §11 of this file.

---

## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)

- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
- **The Week-3 threshold migration already added the schema seams (done).** It landed `check.kind` (default `'expectation'`), `results.metric_value` (NUMERIC) + `duration_ms` (INT), and the severity thresholds — see ADR `0012`. `metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; **don't store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`** (you can't `AVG()`/`STDDEV()` it for trends or anomaly baselines), and **don't add a second migration re-introducing these columns**.
- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.

---

## 11. What NOT to do

- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
- ❌ Don't deepen Azure lock-in: no reading Entra/OIDC provider claims in route/service code (depend on the generic `get_current_user`), no hardcoded Azure resource names/endpoints in business logic, no Azure-only assumptions baked into container images. Azure is one impl behind each seam — see ADR [0010](docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) / [0013](docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md).
- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` / `.env.app.example` as the templates.
- ❌ Don't put a credential — **even a local/mock one** — in any git-tracked file (templates, `scripts/`, CI, compose). Env templates ship the secret keys **blank** with the shape in a comment; `scripts/setup.sh` generates the local-dev password into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app` on first run. Non-secret config defaults and non-secret identifiers (db/user name) may stay populated.
- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
- ❌ **Don't dismiss a finding because it's pre-existing.** DataQ is in production — a defect that predates your change is live for users right now, so its age is irrelevant to whether it matters. Every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never "noted in a review reply" or "documented in a docstring" (CONTRIBUTING rule 3a). Concluding it is genuinely not a defect is fine, but record the determination and evidence — verified-benign is a valid outcome, unexamined is not.
- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
- ❌ Don't add a dependency under a strong-copyleft or source-available license (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL/Elastic, Commons-Clause) — DataQ ships MIT (ADR [0031](docs/adr/0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md), CONTRIBUTING rule 40); weak copyleft (LGPL/MPL) is OK with notices. Exceptions need an ADR.
- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.

---

## 12. Where things live

| Artifact | Location |
|---|---|
| Product roadmap (100 tasks, 8 weeks) | [context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md](context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md) |
| System architecture diagram | [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) |
| Architecture Decision Records | [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) |

### Client-side MCP servers (`.mcp.json`)

Distinct from DataQ's **own** FastMCP server at `/mcp` (ADR 0008 — the 8 tools DataQ *serves* to AI clients), the repo-root **`.mcp.json`** configures MCP servers that AI assistants working in this repo *consume*:

| Server | Package (pinned major) | Publisher | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context7` | `@upstash/context7-mcp@1` (npx) | Upstash | Up-to-date library docs lookup while coding |
| `azure` | `@azure/mcp@3.0.0-beta.29` (npx) — **exact**, see caveats | Microsoft (`github.com/microsoft/mcp`) | Container Apps / Key Vault / Monitor + App Insights KQL without hand-rolled `az rest` — the 2026-07-13 outage was invisible in `/healthz` and only the telemetry showed the exporter log loop |

- **Trust prompt:** Claude Code prompts once per machine before starting servers from a project `.mcp.json`; approve only if the list above matches what's in the file.
- **Pin majors, not `latest`** — same rationale as the GX pin.
- **Supply-chain cadence:** quarterly audit per CONTRIBUTING.md rule 39 (deprecated/yanked/publisher-transfer check before any bump).
- **`azure` caveats (deliberate, re-check before relying on it):** `@azure/mcp`'s only dist-tag is a **beta** (`3.0.0-beta.29`) — Microsoft-published, but pre-stable, so treat tool-surface changes as expected. **This is the one entry pinned to an exact version, not a major**, and deliberately so: npm excludes prereleases from a bare major range, so `@azure/mcp@3` resolves to *nothing* (`E404 No match found for version 3`) and the server would fail to launch. The "pin majors" rule assumes a package with a stable major; this one has none, so the version moves only on a conscious bump. It authenticates through the **local `az` CLI credential**, so it inherits whatever that identity can do — use it for reading state, and keep the Key Vault rule intact: **never surface or print a secret value**. Microsoft telemetry is disabled via `AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=false` in the server env. It is only useful while the Azure estate is up — drop the entry if the wind-down completes.

**Not added, and why** (so the decision isn't re-litigated): a **Postgres MCP** was evaluated for run/result triage and rejected on supply-chain grounds. The reference `@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres` is **deprecated**; the npm `postgres-mcp` is published by a single unaffiliated maintainer; the PyPI `postgres-mcp` declares **no license**, which CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 forbids outright. `psql` over Bash already covers the need with zero added surface.

input.description: Fix OTel severity bug in PR 1312 (#1261)
input.prompt:
You're working in the DataQ repo. PR #1312 (branch `fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade`, fixes #1261) is open with CI presumably green, but an independent review pass found a real, verified correctness bug in it that must be fixed before merge.

```
git fetch origin fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade
git checkout fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade
```

## Background

#1261 moved a log-level downgrade (for exceptions already logged with a full traceback elsewhere, per #1226/#1260) out of two per-caller checks into a new structlog processor `_downgrade_already_logged_exceptions` in `backend/app/core/logging.py`, wired into `shared_processors` (used both as the native structlog processor chain and as `ProcessorFormatter`'s `foreign_pre_chain`). Both callers (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) were simplified back to unconditional `log.exception(...)`.

## The bug (verified empirically by an independent reviewer, reproduce it yourself first)

`log.exception(...)` on a `structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger` is hardcoded to call the underlying stdlib `logging.Logger.exception()` method — which is `self.error(msg, exc_info=True)` under the hood. This sets `LogRecord.levelno = ERROR (40)` and populates `LogRecord.exc_info` with the real traceback **at record-creation time**, completely independent of what any structlog processor later writes into `event_dict["level"]`. The processor's rewrite of `event_dict["level"]` to `"warning"` only affects the JSON body rendered by `JSONRenderer()` for the STDOUT handler — it has zero effect on the actual `logging.LogRecord` object that OTHER handlers attached to the root logger receive.

`backend/app/core/logging.py`'s `_configure_otel_log_export` attaches a second handler (`_RedactingOTelLogHandler`, a `LoggingHandler` subclass from `opentelemetry.sdk._logs`) to the SAME root logger, which exports records to App Insights/OTLP. That handler's `_translate`/`_get_attributes` read `record.levelno` and `record.exc_info` directly off the raw `LogRecord` — NOT the structlog-processed `event_dict`. So for a "downgraded" exception:
- stdout JSON correctly shows `"level": "warning"` (what the new tests check via `capsys`, so they pass)
- but the OTel/App Insights export still reports **ERROR severity** (`severity_number` computed from `record.levelno=40`) and ships the **full traceback** as `exception.type`/`exception.message`/`exception.stacktrace` attributes (read from `record.exc_info`, which the structlog processor never touched — it only popped `event_dict["exc_info"]`, a completely different object)

This silently reintroduces the exact duplicate-alert-noise problem #1226 was meant to eliminate, just on the telemetry channel instead of stdout — invisible to the covering tests because they only assert against captured stdout, never against an actual OTel exporter/handler.

Reproduce it yourself: read `_RedactingOTelLogHandler` (`backend/app/core/logging.py`, search for the class) and confirm it inherits `emit()`/`_translate()` from the SDK's `LoggingHandler` without overriding either — only `_get_attributes` is overridden, and that's for PII redaction, unrelated to severity/exc_info.

## Fix direction

The OTel handler needs to independently consult the SAME `was_already_logged` marker and downgrade the RAW `LogRecord` (not just the structlog event_dict) before it gets translated/exported. Concretely: override `emit()` (or another suitable hook) on `_RedactingOTelLogHandler` to check whether `record.exc_info` carries an exception for which `was_already_logged(exc)` is true, and if so, mutate `record.levelno` to `logging.WARNING` and clear `record.exc_info` (and whatever else `_translate`/`_get_attributes` read that would otherwise leak the traceback) BEFORE calling `super().emit(record)`.

To avoid duplicating the "extract the exception from whatever exc_info shape we have, then check was_already_logged" logic between this handler and the existing `_downgrade_already_logged_exceptions` structlog processor, factor the shared bit (extracting the exception instance + checking the marker) into one small helper both call — you already have `_extract_exc_info_exception` in the same file for exactly this extraction; reuse it (its docstring says it mirrors structlog's own exc_info shape handling, but a raw `LogRecord.exc_info` is always the 3-tuple shape or `None`, so check whether it needs adjustment to also handle that directly, or whether you should call it with `record.exc_info` as-is).

Write a test that actually proves this: construct a `LoggingHandler`-shaped scenario (or the real `_RedactingOTelLogHandler` with a fake/mock exporter capturing exported `LogRecord`/attributes) where a marked exception is logged via `log.exception(...)`, and assert the record/attributes that reach the (mocked) exporter show WARNING severity and no exception attributes — not just that stdout JSON looks right. You're working in the DataQ repo. PR #1312 (branch `fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade`, fixes #1261) is open with CI presumably green, but an independent review pass found a real, verified correctness bug in it that must be fixed before merge.

```
git fetch origin fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade
git checkout fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade
```

## Background

#1261 moved a log-level downgrade (for exceptions already logged with a full traceback elsewhere, per #1226/#1260) out of two per-caller checks into a new structlog processor `_downgrade_already_logged_exceptions` in `backend/app/core/logging.py`, wired into `shared_processors` (used both as the native structlog processor chain and as `ProcessorFormatter`'s `foreign_pre_chain`). Both callers (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) were simplified back to unconditional `log.exception(...)`.

## The bug (verified empirically by an independent reviewer, reproduce it yourself first)

`log.exception(...)` on a `structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger` is hardcoded to call the underlying stdlib `logging.Logger.exception()` method — which is `self.error(msg, exc_info=True)` under the hood. This sets `LogRecord.levelno = ERROR (40)` and populates `LogRecord.exc_info` with the real traceback **at record-creation time**, completely independent of what any structlog processor later writes into `event_dict["level"]`. The processor's rewrite of `event_dict["level"]` to `"warning"` only affects the JSON body rendered by `JSONRenderer()` for the STDOUT handler — it has zero effect on the actual `logging.LogRecord` object that OTHER handlers attached to the root logger receive.

`backend/app/core/logging.py`'s `_configure_otel_log_export` attaches a second handler (`_RedactingOTelLogHandler`, a `LoggingHandler` subclass from `opentelemetry.sdk._logs`) to the SAME root logger, which exports records to App Insights/OTLP. That handler's `_translate`/`_get_attributes` read `record.levelno` and `record.exc_info` directly off the raw `LogRecord` — NOT the structlog-processed `event_dict`. So for a "downgraded" exception:
- stdout JSON correctly shows `"level": "warning"` (what the new tests check via `capsys`, so they pass)
- but the OTel/App Insights export still reports **ERROR severity** (`severity_number` computed from `record.levelno=40`) and ships the **full traceback** as `exception.type`/`exception.message`/`exception.stacktrace` attributes (read from `record.exc_info`, which the structlog processor never touched — it only popped `event_dict["exc_info"]`, a completely different object)

This silently reintroduces the exact duplicate-alert-noise problem #1226 was meant to eliminate, just on the telemetry channel instead of stdout — invisible to the covering tests because they only assert against captured stdout, never against an actual OTel exporter/handler.

Reproduce it yourself: read `_RedactingOTelLogHandler` (`backend/app/core/logging.py`, search for the class) and confirm it inherits `emit()`/`_translate()` from the SDK's `LoggingHandler` without overriding either — only `_get_attributes` is overridden, and that's for PII redaction, unrelated to severity/exc_info.

<result>Monitor stopped, as requested. Work on issue #936 is complete.

**Summary of the fix (PR #1311):**

- **Root cause**: `core_table`'s 3-part (`catalog.schema.table`) form embedded catalog+schema as one unquoted string, so #476's mixed-case quoting fix never reached the catalog/schema — only the table.
- **Fix**: `core_table` gained an optional `dialect` parameter (required only when `catalog` is given). Each of catalog/schema/table is now individually run through the same case-based quoting decision as `folding_identifier`, quoted via the dialect's own `identifier_preparer.quote_identifier` when needed, and folded into Core's table-name slot with `schema=None` — necessary because Snowflake's own SQLAlchemy dialect re-splits a dotted `schema=` string and silently undoes pre-quoting there.
- **Threaded through**: `datasources/monitors.py` (`qualified_table` → `build_monitor_statement` → `evaluate_monitors` → `run_monitors_over_engine`, using `engine.dialect`), `services/anomaly.py` (`measure_metric`, using `conn.dialect`), `services/profile_service.py` (`_table` and its three query builders, using `conn.dialect`), and — found by the mandatory `/code-review` pass and confirmed via a real CI failure — `services/dataset_reader.py`'s `_sql_read` (the ADR-0015 comparison-kind read path), which had been missed initially.
- **Tests**: pinning test inverted, plus new coverage proving the fix against the *real* Snowflake and Databricks dialects (not just the default), a lower-case compatibility test, and a missing-dialect rejection test.
- **Verification**: All directly affected test modules pass locally (472+ tests across `test_sql.py`, `test_monitors.py`, `test_anomaly.py`, `test_profile_service.py`, `test_suites.py`, `test_dataset_reader.py`, plus UC/Snowflake runner tests). Each of catalog/schema/table is now individually run through the same case-based quoting decision as `folding_identifier`, quoted via the dialect's own `identifier_preparer.quote_identifier` when needed, and folded into Core's table-name slot with `schema=None` — necessary because Snowflake's own SQLAlchemy dialect re-splits a dotted `schema=` string and silently undoes pre-quoting there.
- **Threaded through**: `datasources/monitors.py` (`qualified_table` → `build_monitor_statement` → `evaluate_monitors` → `run_monitors_over_engine`, using `engine.dialect`), `services/anomaly.py` (`measure_metric`, using `conn.dialect`), `services/profile_service.py` (`_table` and its three query builders, using `conn.dialect`), and — found by the mandatory `/code-review` pass and confirmed via a real CI failure — `services/dataset_reader.py`'s `_sql_read` (the ADR-0015 comparison-kind read path), which had been missed initially.
- **Tests**: pinning test inverted, plus new coverage proving the fix against the *real* Snowflake and Databricks dialects (not just the default), a lower-case compatibility test, and a missing-dialect rejection test.
- **Verification**: All directly affected test modules pass locally (472+ tests across `test_sql.py`, `test_monitors.py`, `test_anomaly.py`, `test_profile_service.py`, `test_suites.py`, `test_dataset_reader.py`, plus UC/Snowflake runner tests). ## Summary

Confirmed the bug empirically, but the actual root cause differed from the review's diagnosis — and my first fix attempt (matching the reviewer's exact prescription) did nothing, caught by my own regression test. Traced it further:

- `record.exc_info` is **not** what the reviewer assumed for this app's actual configuration (`structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger` + `LoggerFactory`). For a **foreign** (non-structlog) record it is the real tuple, as claimed. But for a **native** `log.exception(...)` call (what every real DataQ call site uses via `get_logger()`), `record.exc_info` is always `None` — `FilteringBoundLogger.exception()` folds `exc_info=True` into the event_dict as a data key, and the processor chain consumes/drops that key before the underlying stdlib `Logger.error()` call is ever made. Verified with direct instrumentation of the real pipeline.
- What actually stays wrong for a native downgraded call is `record.levelno` (fixed at `ERROR` because `.error()` was the method invoked, independent of the processor chain), which is what `LoggingHandler._translate` reads for `severity_number`. `record.msg` (the fully-processed event_dict, stamped by `wrap_for_formatter`) does carry the correct `"level": "warning"`, so that's the reliable signal for the native-record case.

Fix in `backend/app/core/logging.py`:
- Added `_already_logged_exception()` — factors the "extract exception, check `was_already_logged`" logic out of `_downgrade_already_logged_exceptions`, reused for the foreign-record case.
- Added `_record_marks_already_logged_exception(record)` — branches on record shape: dict `record.msg` (native) checks `record.msg.get("level") == "warning"` alongside `record.levelno >= ERROR`; otherwise (foreign) uses `_already_logged_exception(record.exc_info)`.
- `_RedactingOTelLogHandler.emit()` now shallow-copies the record and downgrades `levelno`/`levelname`/`exc_info`/`exc_text` before calling `super().emit()`, when that helper returns true.
- Confirmed via grep that `root` only ever carries two handlers (stdout `StreamHandler` and this OTel handler), so no other channel needs the fix.

Tests added in `backend/tests/core/test_logging.py` (5 new), asserting against the real exported `LogRecord` via the existing `InMemoryLogRecordExporter` fixture — not stdout:
- marked native exception → `SeverityNumber.WARN`, no traceback in body
- unmarked native exception → stays `SeverityNumber.ERROR`, traceback still in body
- marked foreign exception → `WARN`, and `exception.type/message/stacktrace` attributes stripped
- unmarked foreign exception → stays `ERROR` with attributes intact

Mutation-verified: reverted just the `logging.py` fix and confirmed both marked-exception tests fail (foreign and native), for the expected reason.

Local verification: Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit all clean; `pytest backend/tests/core/ backend/tests/alerting/ backend/tests/test_main.py` → 570 passed, 147 skipped (skips are pre-existing Postgres-dependent tests, unrelated to this change — no local Postgres available in this environment; CI's own Postgres service covers them, confirmed green above).

Note on environment: this worktree already had branch `fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade` checked out in another agent's worktree, so I worked from a differently-named local branch (`work-1261-telemetry-fix`) tracking the same remote branch, then pushed with `git push origin work-1261-telemetry-fix:fix/issue-1261-centralize-traceback-downgrade` — a normal (non-force) push, so PR #1312 now shows the new commit `2db5a762`.

Commit: `2db5a762 fix: also downgrade the raw LogRecord so the OTel export honors #1261`, pushed to PR #1312. CI: all 14 checks green. PR left open, not merged, per instructions.

No other out-of-scope findings surfaced during this work, so no new issue was filed.</result>

But it is a real reordering: a connection is now opened before a validation that used to be connection-free, which also means a warehouse-unreachable error can now mask a config error that used to be reported first. (Previous — **30** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1263](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1263) (closes [#1228](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1228)), [#1265](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1265) (closes [#1221](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1221)), [#1268](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1268) (closes [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253)), [#1269](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1269) (closes [#1230](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1230)), and [#1271](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1271) (closes [#1251](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1251)) all merged — five closes offset by filing [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (the #1221 review's deferred driver-guard finding — `connect_args`'s psycopg2-specific keys have no driver-family guard, a pre-existing gap #1221 amplified rather than introduced) and [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (the #1251 review's repo-wide SecretStore-fake sweep follow-up — corrected from an initial 10-file scope to ~31 files after a second review pass found the first undercounted by roughly 2x). **#1228** (merged earlier this session, its docs recount deferred to this batch — the two remaining lineage abort-instead-of-descend sites in the Snowflake pull, `_from_access_history`'s bare `raise` and a floor-failure-after-successful-traversal path, now skip just the affected tier and return the traversal's own edges as a degraded non-prunable result instead of discarding real observed lineage). **#1221** (DB pool keepalives): a warm pooled connection surviving a silent network partition could hang a read forever — `pool_pre_ping`'s own `SELECT 1` has no OS-level floor under it. Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Delimiter [#934](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/934): all four backend CSV reads (runner, profiler sample, column lister, drift introspection) now sniff per FILE via one `flatfile.read_csv_bytes` seam — a `;`/tab/pipe file used to parse as ONE column named after the whole header, silently. Casing [#937](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/937): **the issue's premise #1 was wrong** — the profiler's Core builders already quoted correctly and `schema_drift` binds the name as a value on purpose; the only unquoted path was `monitors.py`'s f-string, so a mixed-case column was unreachable for freshness monitors and nowhere else. Fixed by returning a Core `Select` executed uncompiled, so the CONNECTION's dialect quotes it — hand-rolled `"` quoting would have been actively wrong on UC, which uses backticks and reads `"..."` as a string literal. **Review caught the fix reintroducing the bug it fixed**: delegating to the compiler inherited the DIALECT's reserved-word set, which isn't the warehouse's — SQLAlchemy reserves `copy`, Snowflake doesn't, so a column stored COPY would have been emitted `"copy"` and stopped resolving, on a path that worked before. `folding_identifier` makes the rule ours and case-only. Deferred + filed: [#936](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/936) (3-part catalog/schema still unquoted — unreachable today, pinned by a test so it reads as a limit not a guarantee) | Theme 7 |

input.new_string: | **Open issues** | **43** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-12 after a two-batch quick-fruit sweep of small `v1.1 Backlog` issues, six PRs total, none merged out of order — each opened, CI-verified, mandatory `/code-review`'d, and (for two of the six) corrected against a real review finding before merge. **Batch 1** — [#1305](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1305) closed [#1264](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1264) (lineage floor-denial message named the wrong grant + a `NoReturn` docstring overstated its own effect — both cosmetic/wording; review's own sibling-bug check found the identical mislabeling also affects the ACCESS_HISTORY tier, left unfixed and filed as [#1309](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1309) since #1264's scope was OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES specifically), [#1306](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1306) closed [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (psycopg2-only `connect_args` keys had no driver guard — added a shared `psycopg_connect_args()` helper; review caught two real bugs in the fix's own first pass, both corrected before merge: a `drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg")` prefix check misclassified a bare `postgresql://` URL as non-psycopg even though SQLAlchemy resolves it to psycopg2 by default — the single most common `DATABASE_URL` shape — silently dropping `connect_timeout`/keepalives for it; and the `options` lock-timeout key was left unconditional with a false "portable across drivers" comment, still crashing a genuinely non-psycopg driver on the exact `TypeError` the guard was built to prevent), [#1308](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1308) closed [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation warnings — `Modal.maskClosable`→`mask.closable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`→`onOpenChange`, `Drawer.width`→`size` — verified against the installed antd 6.5.1 types; review's git-history trace found the `Drawer.width` pattern had already been fixed once codebase-wide by #516, and both new sites were written *after* that PR landed, i.e. a genuine regression with nothing to stop a third recurrence — filed as [#1310](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1310)); **#1307** filed alongside #1305/#1306, a deferred-by-design robustness nit (the #1306 message-substitution's string-equality coupling to the classifier's literal return value). **Batch 2** — [#1311](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1311) closed [#936](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/936) (3-part `catalog.schema.table` names left the catalog/schema unquoted, so a mixed-case Unity Catalog namespace silently folded; fixed by threading an explicit `dialect` through `core_table` and quoting each part via the dialect's own `identifier_preparer` — CI caught a missed third call site, `dataset_reader.py`'s ADR-0015 comparison-kind reader, not found by the original grep sweep, fixed same-PR before merge), [#1312](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1312) closed [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261) (centralized the #1226 already-logged-traceback downgrade into a new structlog processor instead of duplicating the opt-in check per caller; review found the processor only rewrote the *stdout* JSON body, leaving the raw stdlib `LogRecord` — which the OTel/App-Insights export handler reads directly — still at ERROR severity with the full traceback attached, silently reintroducing #1226's duplicate-alert-noise problem on the telemetry channel alone; the first fix attempt, written to the review's literal prescription, did nothing and was caught by its own regression test — the real mechanism turned out to be `record.levelno` staying fixed at the moment `.exception()` is called, independent of anything a processor writes to the event dict, not `record.exc_info` as first assumed; fixed by downgrading the raw record in `_RedactingOTelLogHandler.emit()`, proven with tests against the real exported `LogRecord` via `InMemoryLogRecordExporter`, mutation-verified), [#1313](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1313) closed [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (swept the remaining ~31 files of hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles onto the shared `FakeSecretStore`, generalizing its constructor with `raise_on_get`/`raise_on_set` to match a richer shape one file had already proven; full backend suite green in isolation — an interim run against the shared local test Postgres had shown 70 failures from a `create_all`/`drop_all` collision with another concurrent agent session hitting the same DB, root-caused and ruled out, not a defect in the diff); **#1314** filed alongside #1312, a lower-confidence `LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`-filtering edge case below the review's posting threshold, documented with a docstring caveat rather than silently dropped. (Previous — **45** open repo-wide / **28** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1283](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1283)/[#1287](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1287)/[#1288](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1288) merged

input.command:
gh issue create \
  --title "test_anomaly.py: undefined _FakeStore reference broke main (two independently-merged PRs touched the same file)" \
  --label "bug,test" \
  --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Live regression on `main`, found immediately (docs-only PR #1315's CI failed on backend lint/tests despite touching zero code) and fixed same-session.

## What happened

PR #1311 (fixes #936) and PR #1313 (fixes #1270) both touched `backend/tests/services/test_anomaly.py` and were reviewed/CI-verified independently in parallel, then squash-merged in sequence without either being rebased onto the other's changes first:

- #1313 consolidated every hand-rolled `SecretStore` test double in this file (and ~30 others) onto the shared `FakeSecretStore`, deleting the file's local `_FakeStore` class.
- #1311's branch was cut before #1313 merged, and added a *new* test (`test_measurement_...`, the #936 catalog-quoting regression test) that used the pre-consolidation `_FakeStore()`.

Neither PR's own CI caught this — each was green against its own base. Only the *sequential* result (#1313 then #1311, in that merge order) is broken: `_FakeStore` no longer exists anywhere in the file, so line 431's `secret_store=_FakeStore()` was an undefined name (Ruff F821), and `Backend — lint & format` + `Backend — tests` both failed on any subsequent PR built off `main`.

## Fix

`4e6578b0` on `fix/test-anomaly-fakestore-regression` (PR to follow) swaps `_FakeStore()` for `FakeSecretStore()` — the store is never actually read in that test (the connection open is monkeypatched), so any no-arg-constructible double is equivalent. Verified: 46/46 tests in the file pass, Ruff/Black clean.

## Why this matters going forward

Two PRs modifying the same file, merged independently without either rebasing onto the other's landed state, can each be individually green and still produce a broken `main`. GitHub's squash-merge doesn't require a rebase when there's no textual conflict, so this class of defect is invisible until the next PR's CI runs against the new `main` — which is exactly how it surfaced here (a completely unrelated docs-only PR). No action item beyond awareness; not proposing a process change for something this rare, but recording the mechanism for next time this shape shows up.
EOF
)" 2>&1

The analogy was wrong — `pipeline_runs` is workspace-wide orchestrator telemetry with no suite-ownership concept, whereas a near-miss is derived *wholly* from `trigger_binding` rows, which are suite-owned config the sibling `GET /trigger-bindings` already scopes. The last two were process: the tests drove the write LEAF rather than `orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses`, where the hashed tuple is actually *chosen*, so a change there could have desynced read from write and shipped green (a round-trip test through the real write path now covers it); and four new `assert client.get(...)` calls would have been deleted whole by `python -O` — caught by the #787 `test_assert_hygiene` guard, which is exactly what it is for. **CI caught one more that three green local runs did not**: splitting the near-miss resilience assertions into two `it`s failed the shared frontend run with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then')` AFTER all 92 files reported green — a late effect re-invoking the cleared mock. The file's own docstring had documented that exact hazard; the lesson recorded is to check the **exit code**, not the "N passed" line.))))))) |
